binding.description: Example ICD10 Diagnostic codes.

element.short: Timing or nature of the diagnosis
element.definition: When the condition was observed or the relative ranking.
element.comment: For example: admitting, primary, secondary, discharge.
element.requirements: Often required to capture a particular diagnosis, for example: primary or discharge.

binding.description: The type of the diagnosis: admitting, principal, discharge.

element.definition: Indication of whether the diagnosis was present on admission to a facility.
element.requirements: Many systems need to understand for adjudication if the diagnosis was present a time of admission.

binding.description: Present on admission.

element.definition: Procedures performed on the patient relevant to the billing items with the claim.
element.requirements: The specific clinical invention are sometimes required to be provided to justify billing a greater than customary amount for a service.

element.definition: A number to uniquely identify procedure entries.
element.requirements: Necessary to provide a mechanism to link to claim details.

element.definition: When the condition was observed or the relative ranking.
element.comment: For example: primary, secondary.
element.requirements: Often required to capture a particular diagnosis, for example: primary or discharge.

binding.description: Example procedure type codes.

element.definition: Date and optionally time the procedure was performed.
element.requirements: Required for auditing purposes.

element.definition: The code or reference to a Procedure resource which identifies the clinical intervention performed.
element.requirements: This identifies the actual clinical procedure.

constraint.human: Either a concept or a reference is provided but not both.

binding.description: Example ICD10 Procedure codes.

element.definition: Unique Device Identifiers associated with this line item.
element.requirements: The UDI code allows the insurer to obtain device level information on the product supplied.

element.definition: Financial instruments for reimbursement for the health care products and services specified on the claim.
element.comment: All insurance coverages for the patient which may be applicable for reimbursement, of the products and services listed in the claim, are typically provided in the claim to allow insurers to confirm the ordering of the insurance coverages relative to local 'coordination of benefit' rules. One coverage (and only one) with 'focal=true' is to be used in the adjudication of this claim. Coverages appearing before the focal Coverage in the list, and where 'Coverage.subrogation=false', should provide a reference to the ClaimResponse containing the adjudication results of the prior claim.
element.requirements: At least one insurer is required for a claim to be a claim.

element.definition: A number to uniquely identify insurance entries and provide a sequence of coverages to convey coordination of benefit order.
element.requirements: To maintain order of the coverages.

element.short: Coverage to be used for adjudication
element.definition: A flag to indicate that this Coverage is to be used for adjudication of this claim when set to true.
element.comment: A patient may (will) have multiple insurance policies which provide reimbursement for healthcare services and products. For example a person may also be covered by their spouse's policy and both appear in the list (and may be from the same insurer). This flag will be set to true for only one of the listed policies and that policy will be used for adjudicating this claim. Other claims would be created to request adjudication against the other listed policies.
element.requirements: To identify which coverage in the list is being used to adjudicate this claim.

element.definition: The business identifier to be used when the claim is sent for adjudication against this insurance policy.
element.comment: Only required in jurisdictions where insurers, rather than the provider, are required to send claims to  insurers that appear after them in the list. This element is not required when 'subrogation=true'.
element.requirements: This will be the claim number should it be necessary to create this claim in the future. This is provided so that payers may forward claims to other payers in the Coordination of Benefit for adjudication rather than the provider being required to initiate each adjudication.

element.definition: Reference to the insurance card level information contained in the Coverage resource. The coverage issuing insurer will use these details to locate the patient's actual coverage within the insurer's information system.
element.requirements: Required to allow the adjudicator to locate the correct policy and history within their information system.

element.definition: A business agreement number established between the provider and the insurer for special business processing purposes.
element.requirements: Providers may have multiple business arrangements with a given insurer and must supply the specific contract number for adjudication.

element.definition: Reference numbers previously provided by the insurer to the provider to be quoted on subsequent claims containing services or products related to the prior authorization.
element.comment: This value is an alphanumeric string that may be provided over the phone, via text, via paper, or within a ClaimResponse resource and is not a FHIR Identifier.
element.requirements: Providers must quote previously issued authorization reference numbers in order to obtain adjudication as previously advised on the Preauthorization.

element.definition: The result of the adjudication of the line items for the Coverage specified in this insurance.
element.comment: Must not be specified when 'focal=true' for this insurance.
element.requirements: An insurer need the adjudication results from prior insurers to determine the outstanding balance remaining by item for the items in the curent claim.

element.definition: Details of an accident which resulted in injuries which required the products and services listed in the claim.
element.requirements: When healthcare products and services are accident related, benefits may be payable under accident provisions of policies, such as automotive, etc before they are payable under normal health insurance.

element.definition: Date of an accident event  related to the products and services contained in the claim.
element.comment: The date of the accident has to precede the dates of the products and services but within a reasonable timeframe.
element.requirements: Required for audit purposes and adjudication.

element.definition: The type or context of the accident event for the purposes of selection of potential insurance coverages and determination of coordination between insurers.
element.requirements: Coverage may be dependant on the type of accident.

binding.description: Type of accident: work place, auto, etc.

element.definition: The physical location of the accident event.
element.requirements: Required for audit purposes and determination of applicable insurance liability.

element.definition: The amount paid by the patient, in total at the claim claim level or specifically for the item and detail level, to the provider for goods and services.

element.definition: CareTeam members related to this service or product.
element.requirements: Need to identify the individuals and their roles in the provision of the product or service.

element.definition: Diagnosis applicable for this service or product.
element.requirements: Need to related the product or service to the associated diagnoses.

element.definition: Procedures applicable for this service or product.
element.requirements: Need to provide any listed specific procedures to support the product or service being claimed.

element.definition: Exceptions, special conditions and supporting information applicable for this service or product.
element.requirements: Need to reference the supporting information items that relate directly to this product or service.

element.definition: The type of revenue or cost center providing the product and/or service.
element.requirements: Needed in the processing of institutional claims.

binding.description: Codes for the revenue or cost centers supplying the service and/or products.

element.definition: Code to identify the general type of benefits under which products and services are provided.
element.comment: Examples include Medical Care, Periodontics, Renal Dialysis, Vision Coverage.
element.requirements: Needed in the processing of institutional claims as this allows the insurer to determine whether a facial X-Ray is for dental, orthopedic, or facial surgery purposes.

binding.description: Benefit categories such as: oral-basic, major, glasses.

element.short: Billing, service, product, or drug code
element.definition: When the value is a group code then this item collects a set of related item details, otherwise this contains the product, service, drug or other billing code for the item. This element may be the start of a range of .productOrService codes used in conjunction with .productOrServiceEnd or it may be a solo element where .productOrServiceEnd is not used.
element.comment: If this is an actual service or product line, i.e. not a Group, then use code to indicate the Professional Service or Product supplied (e.g. CTP, HCPCS, USCLS, ICD10, NCPDP, DIN, RxNorm, ACHI, CCI). element.requirements: Necessary to state what was provided or done.

binding.description: Allowable service and product codes.

element.short: End of a range of codes
element.definition: This contains the end of a range of product, service, drug or other billing codes for the item. This element is not used when the .productOrService is a group code. This value may only be present when a .productOfService code has been provided to convey the start of the range. Typically this value may be used only with preauthorizations and not with claims.

element.requirements: Most adjudication categories convey a monetary amount.

element.definition: A non-monetary value associated with the category. Mutually exclusive to the amount element above.
element.comment: For example: eligible percentage or co-payment percentage.
element.requirements: Some adjudication categories convey a percentage or a fixed value.

element.definition: The date and time the adjudication decision occured.
element.comment: Implementation Guide authors may choose to require this element based on local regulatory requirements.

element.definition: A claim detail. Either a simple (a product or service) or a 'group' of sub-details which are simple items.
element.requirements: The adjudication for details provided on the claim.

element.definition: A number to uniquely reference the claim detail entry.
element.requirements: Necessary to provide a mechanism to link the adjudication result to the submitted claim detail.

element.definition: Trace number for tracking purposes. May be defined at the jurisdiction level or between trading partners.
element.requirements: Allows partners to uniquely identify components for tracking.

element.definition: The numbers associated with notes below which apply to the adjudication of this item.
element.requirements: Provides a condensed manner for associating human readable descriptive explanations for adjudications on the line item.

element.definition: The high-level results of the adjudication if adjudication has been performed.
The adjudication results.
A sub-detail adjudication of a simple product or service.
element.requirements: The adjudication for sub-details provided on the claim.

element.definition: A number to uniquely reference the claim sub-detail entry.
element.requirements: Necessary to provide a mechanism to link the adjudication result to the submitted claim sub-detail.

element.definition: Trace number for tracking purposes. May be defined at the jurisdiction level or between trading partners.
element.requirements: Allows partners to uniquely identify components for tracking.

element.definition: The numbers associated with notes below which apply to the adjudication of this item.
element.requirements: Provides a condensed manner for associating human readable descriptive explanations for adjudications on the line item.

element.definition: The high-level results of the adjudication if adjudication has been performed.
The adjudication results.
The first-tier service adjudications for payer added product or service lines.
element.requirements: Insurers may redefine the provided product or service or may package and/or decompose groups of products and services. The addItems allows the insurer to provide their line item list with linkage to the submitted items/details/sub-details. In a preauthorization the insurer may use the addItem structure to provide additional information on authorized products and services.

element.definition: Claim items which this service line is intended to replace.
element.requirements: Provides references to the claim items.

element.definition: The sequence number of the details within the claim item which this line is intended to replace.
element.requirements: Provides references to the claim details within the claim item.

element.definition: The sequence number of the sub-details within the details within the claim item which this line is intended to replace.
element.requirements: Provides references to the claim sub-details within the claim detail.

element.definition: Trace number for tracking purposes. May be defined at the jurisdiction level or between trading partners.
element.requirements: Allows partners to uniquely identify components for tracking.

element.short: The recipient of the products and services
element.definition: The party to whom the professional services and/or products have been supplied or are being considered and for whom actual for facast reimbursement is sought.
element.comment: Profilers should consider making this element required when the backbone .subject is a group.

element.definition: Exceptions, special conditions and supporting information applicable for this service or product.
element.requirements: Need to reference the supporting information items that relate directly to this product or service.

element.definition: The providers who are authorized for the services rendered to the patient.
element.requirements: Insurer may provide authorization specifically to a restricted set of providers rather than an open authorization.

element.definition: The type of revenue or cost center providing the product and/or service.
element.requirements: Needed in the processing of institutional claims.

binding.description: Codes for the revenue or cost centers supplying the service and/or products.

element.definition: Code to identify the general type of benefits under which products and services are provided.
element.comment: Examples include Medical Care, Periodontics, Renal Dialysis, Vision Coverage.
element.requirements: Needed in the processing of institutional claims as this allows the insurer to determine whether a facial X-Ray is for dental, orthopedic, or facial surgery purposes.

binding.description: Benefit categories such as: oral-basic, major, glasses.

element.short: Billing, service, product, or drug code
element.definition: When the value is a group code then this item collects a set of related item details, otherwise this contains the product, service, drug or other billing code for the item. This element may be the start of a range of .productOrService codes used in conjunction with .productOrServiceEnd or it may be a solo element where .productOrServiceEnd is not used.
element.comment: If this is an actual service or product line, i.e. not a Group, then use code to indicate the Professional Service or Product supplied (e.g. CTP, HCPCS, USCLS, ICD10, NCPDP, DIN, RxNorm, ACHI, CCI). If a grouping item then use a group code to indicate the type of thing being grouped e.g. 'glasses' or 'compound'.
element.requirements: Necessary to state what was provided or done.

binding.description: Allowable service and product codes.

element.short: End of a range of codes
element.definition: This contains the end of a range of product, service, drug or other billing codes for the item. This element is not used when the .productOrService is a group code. This value may only be present when a .productOfService code has been provided to convey the start of the range. Typically this value may be used only with preauthorizations and not with claims.
alias: End of a range of Drug Code; Bill Code; Service Code

element.definition: Request or Referral for Goods or Service to be rendered.
element.requirements: May identify the service to be provided or provider authorization for the service.

element.definition: Item typification or modifiers codes to convey additional context for the product or service.
element.comment: For example in Oral whether the treatment is cosmetic or associated with TMJ, or for Medical whether the treatment was outside the clinic or outside of office hours.
element.requirements: To support inclusion of the item for adjudication or to charge an elevated fee.

binding.description: Item type or modifiers codes, eg for Oral whether the treatment is cosmetic or associated with TMJ, or an appliance was lost or stolen.

element.short: Program the product or service is provided under
element.definition: Identifies the program under which this may be recovered.
element.comment: For example: Neonatal program, child dental program or drug users recovery program.
element.requirements: Commonly used in in the identification of publicly provided program focused on population segments or disease classifications.

binding.description: Program specific reason codes.

element.short: Date or dates of service or product delivery
element.definition: The date or dates when the service or product was supplied, performed or completed.
element.requirements: Needed to determine whether the  service or product was provided during the term of the insurance coverage.

element.short: Place of service or where product was supplied
element.definition: Where the product or service was provided.
element.requirements: The location can alter whether the item was acceptable for insurance purposes or impact the determination of the benefit amount.

binding.description: Place of service: pharmacy, school, prison, etc.

element.definition: The number of repetitions of a service or product.
element.requirements: Required when the product or service code does not convey the quantity provided.

element.short: Fee, charge or cost per item
element.definition: If the item is not a group then this is the fee for the product or service, otherwise this is the total of the fees for the details of the group.
element.requirements: The amount charged to the patient by the provider for a single unit.

element.definition: A real number that represents a multiplier used in determining the overall value of services delivered and/or goods received. The concept of a Factor allows for a discount or surcharge multiplier to be applied to a monetary amount.
element.comment: To show a 10% senior's discount, the value entered is: 0.90 (1.00 - 0.10).
element.requirements: When discounts are provided to a patient (example: Senior's discount) then this must be documented for adjudication.

element.definition: The total of taxes applicable for this product or service.
element.requirements: Required when taxes are not embedded in the unit price or provided as a separate service.

element.definition: The total amount claimed for the group (if a grouper) or the addItem. Net = unit price * quantity * factor.
element.comment: For example, the formula: quantity * unitPrice * factor  = net. Quantity and factor are assumed to be 1 if not supplied.
element.requirements: Provides the total amount claimed  for the group (if a grouper) or the line item.

element.definition: Physical location where the service is performed or applies.
Physical service site on the patient (limb, tooth, etc.).
element.comment: For example: Providing a tooth code allows an insurer to identify a provider performing a filling on a tooth that was previously removed.
element.requirements: Allows insurer to validate specific procedures.

element.definition: A region or surface of the bodySite, e.g. limb region or tooth surface(s).
element.requirements: Allows insurer to validate specific procedures.

The adjudication results.
The adjudication results which are presented at the header level rather than at the line-item or add-item levels.
element.requirements: Some insurers will receive line-items but provide the adjudication only at a summary or header-level.

element.definition: Categorized monetary totals for the adjudication.
element.comment: Totals for amounts submitted, co-pays, benefits payable etc.
element.requirements: To provide the requestor with financial totals by category for the adjudication.

element.definition: A code to indicate the information type of this adjudication record. Information types may include: the value submitted, maximum values or percentages allowed or payable under the plan, amounts that the patient is responsible for in aggregate or pertaining to this item, amounts paid by other coverages, and the benefit payable for this item.
element.comment: For example codes indicating: Co-Pay, deductible, eligible, benefit, tax, etc.
element.requirements: Needed to convey the type of total provided.

binding.description: The adjudication codes.

element.definition: Monetary total amount associated with the category.
element.requirements: Needed to convey the total monetary amount.

element.definition: Payment details for the adjudication of the claim.
element.requirements: Needed to convey references to the financial instrument that has been used if payment has been made.

element.definition: Whether this represents partial or complete payment of the benefits payable.
element.requirements: To advise the requestor when the insurer believes all payments to have been completed.

binding.description: The type (partial, complete) of the payment.

element.definition: Total amount of all adjustments to this payment included in this transaction which are not related to this claim's adjudication.
element.comment: Insurers will deduct amounts owing from the provider (adjustment), such as a prior overpayment, from the amount owing to the provider (benefits payable) when payment is made to the provider.
element.requirements: To advise the requestor of adjustments applied to the payment.

element.definition: Reason for the payment adjustment.
element.requirements: Needed to clarify the monetary adjustment.

binding.description: Payment Adjustment reason codes.

element.definition: Estimated date the payment will be issued or the actual issue date of payment.
element.requirements: To advise the payee when payment can be expected.

element.definition: Benefits payable less any payment adjustment.
element.requirements: Needed to provide the actual payment amount.

element.definition: Issuer's unique identifier for the payment instrument.
element.comment: For example: EFT number or check number.
element.requirements: Enable the receiver to reconcile when payment received.

element.definition: A code, used only on a response to a preauthorization, to indicate whether the benefits payable have been reserved and for whom.
element.comment: Fund would be release by a future claim quoting the preAuthRef of this response. Examples of values include: provider, patient, none.
element.requirements: Needed to advise the submitting provider on whether the request for reservation of funds has been honored.

binding.description: For whom funds are to be reserved: (Patient, Provider, None).

element.definition: A code for the form to be used for printing the content.
element.comment: May be needed to identify specific jurisdictional forms.
element.requirements: Needed to specify the specific form used for producing output for this response.

binding.description: The forms codes.

element.definition: The actual form, by reference or inclusion, for printing the content or an EOB.
element.comment: Needed to permit insurers to include the actual form.
element.requirements: Needed to include the specific form used for producing output for this response.

element.definition: A note that describes or explains adjudication results in a human readable form.
element.requirements: Provides the insurer specific textual explanations associated with the processing.

element.definition: A code to indicate the business purpose of the note.
element.requirements: Process Notes may encompass a significant number of kinds of notes. These could be disclaimers (particularly useful for predetermination), a statement about adjudication, a conditional statement, or others.

binding.description: Business class of the process note.

element.definition: A number to uniquely identify a note entry.
element.requirements: Necessary to provide a mechanism to link from adjudications.

element.definition: The business purpose of the note text.
element.requirements: To convey the expectation for when the text is used.

binding.description: The presentation types of notes.

element.definition: The explanation or description associated with the processing.
element.requirements: Required to provide human readable explanation.

element.definition: A code to define the language used in the text of the note.
element.comment: Only required if the language is different from the resource language.
element.requirements: Note text may vary from the resource defined language.

binding.description: IETF language tag for a human language

element.definition: Request for additional supporting or authorizing information.
element.comment: For example: professional reports, documents, images, clinical resources, or accident reports.
element.requirements: Need to communicate insurer request for additional information required to support the adjudication.

element.definition: Financial instruments for reimbursement for the health care products and services specified on the claim.
element.comment: All insurance coverages for the patient which may be applicable for reimbursement, of the products and services listed in the claim, are typically provided in the claim to allow insurers to confirm the ordering of the insurance coverages relative to local 'coordination of benefit' rules. One coverage (and only one) with 'focal=true' is to be used in the adjudication of this claim. Coverages appearing before the focal Coverage in the list, and where 'subrogation=false', should provide a reference to the ClaimResponse containing the adjudication results of the prior claim.
element.requirements: At least one insurer is required for a claim to be a claim.

element.definition: A number to uniquely identify insurance entries and provide a sequence of coverages to convey coordination of benefit order.
element.requirements: To maintain order of the coverages.

element.short: Coverage to be used for adjudication
element.definition: A flag to indicate that this Coverage is to be used for adjudication of this claim when set to true.
element.comment: A patient may (will) have multiple insurance policies which provide reimbursement for healthcare services and products. For example a person may also be covered by their spouse's policy and both appear in the list (and may be from the same insurer). This flag will be set to true for only one of the listed policies and that policy will be used for adjudicating this claim. Other claims would be created to request adjudication against the other listed policies.
element.requirements: To identify which coverage in the list is being used to adjudicate this claim.

element.definition: Reference to the insurance card level information contained in the Coverage resource. The coverage issuing insurer will use these details to locate the patient's actual coverage within the insurer's information system.
element.requirements: Required to allow the adjudicator to locate the correct policy and history within their information system.

element.definition: A business agreement number established between the provider and the insurer for special business processing purposes.
element.requirements: Providers may have multiple business arrangements with a given insurer and must supply the specific contract number for adjudication.

element.definition: The result of the adjudication of the line items for the Coverage specified in this insurance.
element.comment: Must not be specified when 'focal=true' for this insurance.
element.requirements: An insurer need the adjudication results from prior insurers to determine the outstanding balance remaining by item for the items in the curent claim.

element.definition: Errors encountered during the processing of the adjudication.
element.comment: If the request contains errors then an error element should be provided and no adjudication related sections (item, addItem, or payment) should be present.
element.requirements: Need to communicate processing issues to the requestor.

element.definition: The sequence number of the line item submitted which contains the error. This value is omitted when the error occurs outside of the item structure.
element.requirements: Provides references to the claim items.

element.definition: The sequence number of the detail within the line item submitted which contains the error. This value is omitted when the error occurs outside of the item structure.
element.requirements: Provides references to the claim details within the claim item.

element.definition: The sequence number of the sub-detail within the detail within the line item submitted which contains the error. This value is omitted when the error occurs outside of the item structure.
element.requirements: Provides references to the claim sub-details within the claim detail.

element.definition: An error code, from a specified code system, which details why the claim could not be adjudicated.
element.requirements: Required to convey processing errors.

binding.description: The adjudication error codes.

element.short: FHIRPath of element(s) related to issue
element.definition: A [simple subset of FHIRPath](fhirpath.html#simple) limited to element names, repetition indicators and the default child accessor that identifies one of the elements in the resource that caused this issue to be raised.
element.comment: The root of the FHIRPath is the resource or bundle that generated OperationOutcome.  Each FHIRPath SHALL resolve to a single node.
element.requirements: Allows systems to highlight or otherwise guide users to elements implicated in issues to allow them to be fixed more easily.

ClinicalUseDefinition NDomainResourceA single issue - either an indication, contraindication, interaction or an undesirable effect for a medicinal product, medication, device or procedure
+ Rule: Indication, Contraindication, Interaction, UndesirableEffect and Warning cannot be used in the same instance
+ Rule: ClinicalUseDefinition.contraindication can only be used when type is 'contraindication'
+ Rule: ClinicalUseDefinition.indication can only be used when type is 'indication'
+ Rule: ClinicalUseDefinition.undesirableEffect can only be used when type is 'undesirable-effect'
+ Rule: ClinicalUseDefinition.interaction can only be used when type is 'interaction'
+ Rule: ClinicalUseDefinition.warning can only be used when type is 'warning'

Applications processing a resource are required to check for modifier extensions.

Modifier extensions SHALL NOT change the meaning of any elements on Resource or DomainResource (including cannot change the meaning of modifierExtension itself).
element.comment: There can be no stigma associated with the use of extensions by any application, project, or standard - regardless of the institution or jurisdiction that uses or defines the extensions.  The use of extensions is what allows the FHIR specification to retain a core level of simplicity for everyone.
element.requirements: Modifier extensions allow for extensions that *cannot* be safely ignored to be clearly distinguished from the vast majority of extensions which can be safely ignored.  This promotes interoperability by eliminating the need for implementers to prohibit the presence of extensions. For further information, see the [definition of modifier extensions](extensibility.html#modifierExtension).

element.definition: The CodeSystem resource is used to declare the existence of and describe a code system or code system supplement and its key properties, and optionally define a part or all of its content.

constraint.human: Within a code system definition, all the codes SHALL be unique
If there is an explicit hierarchy, a hierarchyMeaning should be provided
If there is an implicit hierarchy, a hierarchyMeaning should be provided
Name should be usable as an identifier for the module by machine processing applications such as code generation
If the code system content = supplement, it must nominate what it's a supplement for

extension.valueMarkdown: There is scope for unsafe interpretation of codes if it's not known whether the CodeSystem is case sensitive or not

constraint.human: caseSensitive SHOULD be provided

element.short: Canonical identifier for this code system, represented as a URI (globally unique) (Coding.system)
element.definition: An absolute URI that is used to identify this code system when it is referenced in a specification, model, design or an instance; also called its canonical identifier. This SHOULD be globally unique and SHOULD be a literal address at which an authoritative instance of this code system is (or will be) published. This URL can be the target of a canonical reference. It SHALL remain the same when the code system is stored on different servers. This is used in [Coding](datatypes.html#Coding).system.
element.comment:
Can be a urn:uuid: or a urn:oid: but real http: addresses are preferred.  Multiple instances may share the same URL if they have a distinct version.

The determination of when to create a new version of a resource (same url, new version) vs. defining a new artifact is up to the author.  Considerations for making this decision are found in [Technical and Business Versions](resource.html#versions). 

In some cases, the resource can no longer be found at the stated url, but the url itself cannot change. Implementations can use the [meta.source](resource.html#meta) element to indicate where the current master source of the resource can be found.
element.requirements: Allows the code system to be referenced by a single globally unique identifier.

constraint.human: URL should not contain | or # - these characters make processing canonical references problematic

element.short: Additional identifier for the code system (business identifier)
element.definition: A formal identifier that is used to identify this code system when it is represented in other formats, or referenced in a specification, model, design or an instance.
element.requirements: Allows externally provided and/or usable business identifiers to be easily associated with the module.

element.short: Business version of the code system (Coding.version)
element.definition: The identifier that is used to identify this version of the code system when it is referenced in a specification, model, design or instance. This is an arbitrary value managed by the code system author and is not expected to be globally unique. For example, it might be a timestamp (e.g. yyyymmdd) if a managed version is not available. There is also no expectation that versions can be placed in a lexicographical sequence. This is used in [Coding](datatypes.html#Coding).version.
element.comment: There may be different code system instances that have the same identifier but different versions.  The version can be appended to the url in a reference to allow a reference to a particular business version of the code system with the format [url]|[version]. The version SHOULD NOT contain a '#' - see [Business Version](resource.html#bv-format).

element.definition: Indicates the mechanism used to compare versions to determine which CodeSystem is more current.
element.comment: If set as a string, this is a FHIRPath expression that has two additional context variables passed in - %version1 and %version2 and will return a negative number if version1 is newer, a positive number if version2 and a 0 if the version ordering can't be successfully be determined.

element.short: Name for this code system (computer friendly)
element.definition: A natural language name identifying the code system. This name should be usable as an identifier for the module by machine processing applications such as code generation.
element.comment: The name is not expected to be globally unique. The name should be a simple alphanumeric type name to ensure that it is machine-processing friendly.
element.requirements: Support human navigation and code generation.

element.short: Name for this code system (human friendly)
element.definition: A short, descriptive, user-friendly title for the code system.
element.comment: This name does not need to be machine-processing friendly and may contain punctuation, white-space, etc.

element.definition: The status of this code system. Enables tracking the life-cycle of the content.
element.comment:
Allows filtering of code systems that are appropriate for use versus not.

See guidance around (not) making local changes to elements [here](canonicalresource.html#localization).
element.isModifierReason: This is labeled as "Is Modifier" because applications should not use a retired CodeSystem without due consideration

binding.description: The lifecycle status of an artifact.

element.short: For testing only - never for real usage
element.definition: A Boolean value to indicate that this code system is authored for testing purposes (or education/evaluation/marketing) and no version of this resource will ever be intended for genuine usage.
element.comment:
Allows filtering of code systems that are appropriate for use versus not.. Experimental resources might include example instances in implementation guides, instances created solely for testing purposes, etc. If experimental is 'true' for any version of a resource, it should be true for all versions of the resource.  (If experimental changes, then it is being misused or a resource that was never intended for real-world use has unexpectedly changed its purpose.).

Experimental resources are not expected to be stable and may well have breaking changes without a corresponding change to the 'version' element.
element.requirements: Enables experimental content to be developed following the same lifecycle that would be used for a production-level code system.
element.meaningWhenMissing: If absent, this resource is treated as though it is not experimental.

element.definition: The date  (and optionally time) when the code system was last significantly changed. The date must change when the business version changes and it must change if the status code changes. In addition, it should change when the substantive content of the code system changes.
element.comment:
The date is often not tracked until the resource is published, but may be present on draft content. Note that this is not the same as the resource last-modified-date, since the resource may be a secondary representation of the code system. Additional specific dates may be added as extensions or be found by consulting Provenances associated with past versions of the resource.

See guidance around (not) making local changes to elements [here](canonicalresource.html#localization).

element.short: Name of the publisher/steward (organization or individual)
element.definition: The name of the organization or individual responsible for the release and ongoing maintenance of the code system.
element.comment: Usually an organization but may be an individual. The publisher (or steward) of the code system is the organization or individual primarily responsible for the maintenance and upkeep of the code system. This is not necessarily the same individual or organization that developed and initially authored the content. The publisher is the primary point of contact for questions or issues with the code system. This item SHOULD be populated unless the information is available from context.
element.requirements: Helps establish the "authority/credibility" of the code system.  May also allow for contact.

element.definition: Contact details to assist a user in finding and communicating with the publisher.
element.comment:
May be a web site, an email address, a telephone number, etc.

See guidance around (not) making local changes to elements [here](canonicalresource.html#localization).

element.short: Natural language description of the code system
element.definition: A free text natural language description of the code system from a consumer's perspective.
element.comment: This description can be used to capture details such as comments about misuse, instructions for clinical use and interpretation, literature references, examples from the paper world, etc. It is not a rendering of the code system as conveyed in the 'text' field of the resource itself. This item SHOULD be populated unless the information is available from context (e.g. the language of the code system is presumed to be the predominant language in the place the code system was created).

element.short: The context that the content is intended to support
element.definition: The content was developed with a focus and intent of supporting the contexts that are listed. These contexts may be general categories (gender, age, ...) or may be references to specific programs (insurance plans, studies, ...) and may be used to assist with indexing and searching for appropriate code system instances.
element.comment: When multiple useContexts are specified, there is no expectation that all or any of the contexts apply.
element.requirements: Assist in searching for appropriate content.

element.short: Jurisdiction of the authority that maintains the code system (if applicable)
element.definition: A legal or geographic region in which the authority that maintains the resource is operating.  In general, the jurisdiction is also found in the useContext.  The useContext may reference additional jurisdictions because the defining jurisdiction does not necessarily limit the jurisdictions of use.
element.comment: It may be possible for the code system to be used in jurisdictions other than those for which it was originally designed or intended.

binding.description: Countries and regions within which this artifact is targeted for use.

element.short: Why this code system is defined
element.definition: Explanation of why this code system is needed and why it has been designed as it has.
element.comment: This element does not describe the usage of the code system. Instead, it provides traceability of ''why'' the resource is either needed or ''why'' it is defined as it is.  This may be used to point to source materials or specifications that drove the structure of this code system.

element.short: Notice about intellectual property ownership, can include restrictions on use
element.definition: A copyright statement relating to the code system and/or its contents. Copyright statements are notices of intellectual property ownership and can include restrictions on the use and publishing of the code system.
element.comment: ... Sometimes, the copyright differs between the code system and the codes that are included. The copyright statement should clearly differentiate between these when required.
element.requirements: Consumers must be able to determine any legal restrictions on the use of the code system and/or its content.

element.definition: A short string (<50 characters), suitable for inclusion in a page footer that identifies the copyright holder, effective period, and optionally whether rights are restricted. (e.g. 'All rights reserved', 'Some rights reserved').
element.comment: The copyright symbol and the '(c)' textual representation SHOULD NOT be included in this string. It will be added by software when rendering the notation. Full details about licensing, restrictions, warrantees, etc. goes in the more general 'copyright' element.
element.requirements: Defines the content expected to be rendered in all representations of the artifact.

element.short: When the CodeSystem was approved by publisher
element.definition: The date on which the resource content was approved by the publisher. Approval happens once when the content is officially approved for usage.
element.comment:
The 'date' element may be more recent than the approval date because of minor changes or editorial corrections.

See guidance around (not) making local changes to elements [here](canonicalresource.html#localization).

element.short: When the CodeSystem was last reviewed by the publisher
element.definition: The date on which the resource content was last reviewed. Review happens periodically after approval but does not change the original approval date.
element.comment:
If specified, this date follows the original approval date.

See guidance around (not) making local changes to elements [here](canonicalresource.html#localization).
element.requirements: Gives a sense of how "current" the content is.  Resources that have not been reviewed in a long time may have a risk of being less appropriate/relevant.

element.short: When the CodeSystem is expected to be used
element.definition: The period during which the CodeSystem content was or is planned to be in active use.
element.comment:
The effective period for a CodeSystem  determines when the content is applicable for usage and is independent of publication and review dates. For example, a system intended to be used for the year 2016 might be published in 2015.

See guidance around (not) making local changes to elements [here](canonicalresource.html#localization).
element.requirements: Allows establishing a transition before a resource comes into effect and also allows for a sunsetting  process when new versions of the CodeSystem are or are expected to be used instead.

element.definition: Descriptions related to the content of the CodeSystem. Topics provide a high-level categorization as well as keywords for the CodeSystem that can be useful for filtering and searching.
element.requirements: Repositories must be able to determine how to categorize the CodeSystem so that it can be found by topical and keyword searches.

element.definition: An individual or organization primarily involved in the creation and maintenance of the CodeSystem.
An individual or organization primarily responsible for internal coherence of the CodeSystem.
An individual or organization asserted by the publisher to be primarily responsible for review of some aspect of the CodeSystem.
element.comment: See guidance around (not) making local changes to elements [here](canonicalresource.html#localization).

element.definition: An individual or organization asserted by the publisher to be responsible for officially endorsing the CodeSystem for use in some setting.
element.comment: See guidance around (not) making local changes to elements [here](canonicalresource.html#localization).

element.definition: Related artifacts such as additional documentation, justification, dependencies, bibliographic references, and predecessor and successor artifacts. If the type is `successor` or `predecessor`, the related resource must be a CodeSystem.
element.comment: Each related artifact is either an attachment, or a reference to another resource, but not both.
element.requirements: A CodeSystem must be able to provide enough information for consumers of the content (and/or interventions or results produced by the content) to be able to determine and understand the justification for and evidence in support of the content.

constraint.human: Related artifact can't be depends-on or composed-of

element.short: If code comparison is case sensitive
element.definition: If code comparison is case sensitive when codes within this system are compared to each other.
element.comment: If this value is missing, then it is not specified whether a code system is case sensitive or not. When case sensitivity is not known, systems SHOULD produce codes with the correct case, and treat codes as case-sensitive, since this will mean any incorrect interpretation of codes is not a silent failure. This element is primarily provided to support validation software.  Case-insensitive comparisons do not take locale into account, and will result in unsatisfactory results for certain locales. Character case definitions and conversions are out of scope for the FHIR standard, and the results of such operations are implementation dependent.

element.short: Canonical reference to the value set with entire code system
element.definition: Canonical reference to the value set that contains all codes in the code system independent of code status.
element.comment: The definition of the value set SHALL include all codes from this code system, independent of concept status, and only codes from this code system. It SHALL be immutable, and operations SHOULD support validation of any allowed code compositions.

element.definition: The meaning of the hierarchy of concepts as represented in this resource.
element.comment: Note that other representations might have a different hierarchy or none at all, and represent the information using properties.

binding.description: The meaning of the hierarchy of concepts in a code system.

element.short: If code system defines a compositional grammar
element.definition: The code system defines a compositional (post-coordination) grammar.
element.comment: Note that the code system resource does not define what the compositional grammar is, only whether or not there is one. Note that the code system resource does not define what the compositional grammar is, only whether or not there is one. Review the Using Code System X with HL7 Standards (where Code System X is a specific code system) pages at [terminology.hl7.org](https://terminology.hl7.org/external_code_systems.html) to learn about a code system's post coordination support. [Coding.code](datatypes-definitions.html#Coding.code) has some more information about how a post coordinated expression may be exchanged in a code element.

element.definition: This flag is used to signify that the code system does not commit to concept permanence across versions. If true, a version must be specified when referencing this code system.
element.comment:
Best practice is that code systems do not redefine concepts, or that if concepts are redefined, a new code system definition is created. But this is not always possible, so some code systems may be defined as 'versionNeeded'.

Most code systems occasionally refine the displays defined for concepts between versions. Contexts in which the concept display values are validated may require that the version be specified for some code systems irrespective of the value of this property.

element.definition: The extent of the content of the code system (the concepts and codes it defines) are represented in this resource instance.

binding.description: The extent of the content of the code system (the concepts and codes it defines) are represented in a code system resource.

element.short: Canonical URL of Code System this adds designations and properties to
element.definition: The canonical URL of the code system that this code system supplement is adding designations and properties to.
element.comment: The most common use of a code system supplement is to add additional language support.

element.short: Total concepts in the code system
element.definition: The total number of concepts defined by the code system. Where the code system has a compositional grammar, the basis of this count is defined by the system steward.
element.comment: The count of concepts defined in this resource cannot be more than this value but may be less for several reasons - see the content element.

element.short: Filter that can be used in a value set
element.definition: A filter that can be used in a value set compose statement when selecting concepts using a filter.
element.comment: Note that filters defined in code systems usually require custom code on the part of any terminology engine that will make them available for use in value set filters. For this reason, they are generally only seen in high value published terminologies.

element.definition: The code that identifies this filter when it is used as a filter in [ValueSet](valueset.html#).compose.include.filter.

element.short: How or why the filter is used
element.definition: A description of how or why the filter is used.

element.short: = | is-a | descendent-of | is-not-a | regex | in | not-in | generalizes | child-of | descendent-leaf | exists | property-value-of
element.definition: A list of operators that can be used with the filter.

binding.description: The kind of operation to perform as a part of a property based filter.

element.short: Code from the system, or regex criteria, or boolean value for exists
element.definition: CodeSystem.filter.value is represented as a string, and the string value must be as described in [Using Filter Values](valueset.html#filter-values).

element.short: Additional information supplied about each concept
element.definition: A property defines an additional slot through which additional information can be provided about a concept.
element.comment: Multiple occurrences of CodeSystem.concept.property may occur for a CodeSystem.property where     CodeSystem.concept.property.code is the same and CodeSystem.concept.property.value differs. For example: multiple designations for a single concept.

element.short: Identifies the property on the concepts, and when referred to in operations
element.definition: A code that is used to identify the property. The code is used internally (in CodeSystem.concept.property.code) and also externally, such as in property filters.
Reference to the formal meaning of the property. One possible source of meaning is the [Concept Properties](codesystem-concept-properties.html) code system.
element.comment: The URIs used here SHOULD be drawn from the [Concept Properties](codesystem-concept-properties.html) code system, where the URI string consists of \[code system URL]#\[code]

element.short: Why the property is defined, and/or what it conveys
element.definition: A description of the property- why it is defined, and how its value might be used.

element.short: code | Coding | string | integer | boolean | dateTime | decimal
element.definition: The type of the property value. Properties of type "code" contain a code defined by the code system or another code system.
element.comment: If type is code, and a defined set of codes is to be used, these codes can be specified by using the extension http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition/codesystem-property-valueset

binding.description: The type of a property value.

element.definition: Concepts that are in the code system. The concept definitions are inherently hierarchical, but the definitions must be consulted to determine what the meanings of the hierarchical relationships are.
element.comment: If this is empty, it means that the code system resource does not represent the content of the code system.

constraint.human: If a concept identifies an alternate, there must be a reciprocal relationship

element.definition: A code - a text symbol - that uniquely identifies the concept within the code system.

element.short: Text to display to the user
element.definition: A human readable string that is the recommended default way to present this concept to a user.

The formal definition of the concept. The code system resource does not make formal definitions required, because of the prevalence of legacy systems. However, they are highly recommended, as without them there is no formal meaning associated with the concept.
Additional representations for the concept - other languages, aliases, specialized purposes, used for particular purposes, etc.
element.comment: Concepts have both a ```display``` and an array of ```designation```. The display is equivalent to a special designation with an implied ```designation.use``` of "primary designation" and a language equal to the [Resource Language](resource.html#language).
element.requirements: Many concept definition systems support multiple representations, in multiple languages, and for multiple purposes.

constraint.human: Must have a value for concept.designation.use if concept.designation.additionalUse is present

element.definition: The language this designation is defined for.
element.comment: In the absence of a language, the resource language applies.

binding.description: IETF language tag for a human language

element.short: Details how this designation would be used
element.definition: A code that details how this designation would be used.
element.comment: If no use is provided, the designation can be assumed to be suitable for general display to a human user.

binding.description: Details of how a designation would be used.

element.short: Additional ways how this designation would be used
element.definition: Additional codes that detail how this designation would be used, if there is more than one use.
element.comment: This was added rather than increasing the cardinality of .use to 0..* in order to maintain backward compatibility.

binding.description: Details of how a designation would be used.

element.short: The text value for this designation
element.definition: The text value for this designation.
A property value for this concept.

element.short: Reference to CodeSystem.property.code or a FHIR defined concept-property
element.definition: Identifies a property that is either defined in this CodeSystem (`CodeSystem.property.code`) or is a code from [http://hl7.org/fhir/concept-properties](codesystem.html#defined-props).
element.comment: Note that when the `CodeSystem.property.code` is defined in the CodeSystem itself, there is no mechanism to create a ValueSet, so there is no terminology binding.

element.short: Value of the property for this concept
element.definition: The value of this property.
Defines children of a concept to produce a hierarchy of concepts. The nature of the relationships is variable (is-a/contains/categorizes) - see hierarchyMeaning.

resource.name: Communication
resource.description: A clinical or business level record of information being transmitted or shared; e.g. an alert that was sent to a responsible provider, a public health agency communication to a provider/reporter in response to a case report for a reportable condition.

element.short: A clinical or business level record of information being transmitted or shared
element.definition: A clinical or business level record of information being transmitted or shared; e.g. an alert that was sent to a responsible provider, a public health agency communication to a provider/reporter in response to a case report for a reportable condition.

constraint.human: If the resource is contained in another resource, it SHALL NOT contain nested Resources
If the resource is contained in another resource, it SHALL be referred to from elsewhere in the resource or SHALL refer to the containing resource
constraint.expression: contained.where((('#'+id.trace('id') in %resource.descendants().select(reference | as(uri))) or descendants().where(reference='#' | as(uri)='#').exists()).not()).trace('unmatched', id).empty()

constraint.human: If a resource is contained in another resource, it SHALL NOT have a meta.versionId or a meta.lastUpdated
If a resource is contained in another resource, it SHALL NOT have a security label

extension.valueMarkdown: When a resource has no narrative, only systems that fully understand the data can display the resource to a human safely. Including a human readable representation in the resource makes for a much more robust ecosystem and cheaper handling of resources by intermediary systems. Some ecosystems restrict distribution of resources to only those systems that do fully understand the resources, and as a consequence implementers may believe that the narrative is superfluous. However experience shows that such ecosystems often open up to new participants over time.

constraint.human: A resource should have narrative for robust management

element.definition: The logical id of the resource, as used in the URL for the resource. Once assigned, this value never changes.
element.comment: Within the context of the FHIR RESTful interactions, the resource has an id except for cases like the create and conditional update. Otherwise, the use of the resource id depends on the given use case.

element.definition: The metadata about the resource. This is content that is maintained by the infrastructure. Changes to the content might not always be associated with version changes to the resource.

constraint.human: All FHIR elements must have a @value or children

element.short: A set of rules under which this content was created
element.definition: A reference to a set of rules that were followed when the resource was constructed, and which must be understood when processing the content. Often, this is a reference to an implementation guide that defines the special rules along with other profiles etc. For DomainResources, if more than one implicitRules policy applies, additional policies may be conveyed using the [additionalImplicitRules](https://build.fhir.org/ig/HL7/fhir-extensions/StructureDefinition-additionalImplicitRules.html) extension.
element.comment: Asserting this rule set restricts the content to be only understood by a limited set of trading partners. This inherently limits the usefulness of the data in the long term. However, the existing health eco-system is highly fractured, and not yet ready to define, collect, and exchange data in a generally computable sense. Wherever possible, implementers and/or specification writers should avoid using this element. Often, when used, the URL is a reference to an implementation guide that defines these special rules as part of its narrative along with other profiles, value sets, etc.

constraint.human: All FHIR elements must have a @value or children

element.isModifierReason: This element is labeled as a modifier because the implicit rules may provide additional knowledge about the resource that modifies its meaning or interpretation

element.definition: The base language in which the resource is written.
element.comment: Language is provided to support indexing and accessibility (typically, services such as text to speech use the language tag). The html language tag in the narrative applies  to the narrative. The language tag on the resource may be used to specify the language of other presentations generated from the data in the resource. Not all the content has to be in the base language. The Resource.language should not be assumed to apply to the narrative automatically. If a language is specified, it should it also be specified on the div element in the html (see rules in HTML5 for information about the relationship between xml:lang and the html lang attribute).

constraint.human: All FHIR elements must have a @value or children

Wherever possible, implementers and/or specification writers should avoid using this element. The determination of when to create a new version of a resource (same url, new version) vs. defining a new artifact is up to the author.  Considerations for making this decision are found in [Technical and Business Versions](resource.html#versions). 

In some cases, the resource can no longer be found at the stated url, but the url itself cannot change. Implementations can use the [meta.source](resource.html#meta) element to indicate where the current master source of the resource can be found.

For example, it might be a timestamp (e.g. yyyymmdd) if a managed version is not available. There is also no expectation that versions can be placed in a lexicographical sequence.

resource.name: Composition
resource.description: Composition provides the structural backbone for assembling a set of healthcare-related information into a single logical package that provides a single coherent statement of meaning, establishes its own context and has traceability to the author who is making the statement.
resource.purpose: To support documents, and also to capture the EN13606 notion of an attested commit to the patient EHR, and to allow a set of disparate resources at the information/engineering level to be gathered into a clinical statement.

element.short: A set of resources composed into a single coherent clinical statement with clinical attestation
element.definition: Composition provides the structural backbone for assembling a set of healthcare-related information into a single logical package that provides a single coherent statement of meaning, establishes its own context and has traceability to the author who is making the statement.
element.comment: While the focus of this specification is on patient-specific clinical statements, this resource can also apply to other healthcare-related statements such as study protocol designs, healthcare invoices and other activities that are not necessarily patient-specific or clinical.

If the resource is contained in another resource, it SHALL be referred to from elsewhere in the resource or SHALL refer to the containing resource

If a resource is contained in another resource, it SHALL NOT have a security label

extension.valueMarkdown: When a resource has no narrative, only systems that fully understand the data can display the resource to a human safely. Including a human readable representation in the resource makes for a much more robust ecosystem and cheaper handling of resources by intermediary systems. Some ecosystems restrict distribution of resources to only those systems that do fully understand the resources, and as a consequence implementers may believe that the narrative is superfluous. However experience shows that such ecosystems often open up to new participants over time.

element.short: A set of resources composed into a single coherent clinical statement with clinical attestation
element.definition: Composition provides the structural backbone for assembling a set of healthcare-related information into a single logical package that provides a single coherent statement of meaning, establishes its own context and has traceability to the author who is making the statement.
element.comment: While the focus of this specification is on patient-specific clinical statements, this resource can also apply to other healthcare-related statements such as study protocol designs, healthcare invoices and other activities that are not necessarily patient-specific or clinical.

element.short: Canonical identifier for this Composition, represented as a URI (globally unique)
element.definition: An absolute URI that is used to identify this Composition when it is referenced in a specification, model, design or an instance; also called its canonical identifier. This SHOULD be globally unique and SHOULD be a literal address at which an authoritative instance of this Composition is (or will be) published. This URL can be the target of a canonical reference. It SHALL remain the same when the Composition is stored on different servers.
element.comment: Can be a urn:uuid: or a urn:oid: but real http: addresses are preferred. Multiple instances may share the same URL if they have a distinct version.
element.requirements: Allows the Composition to be referenced by a single globally unique identifier.

element.definition: A version-independent identifier for the Composition. This identifier stays constant as the composition is changed over time.
element.comment: Similar to ClinicalDocument/setId in CDA. See discussion in resource definition for how these relate.

element.short: An explicitly assigned identifier of a variation of the content in the Composition
element.definition: An explicitly assigned identifier of a variation of the content in the Composition.
element.comment: This element is the author-assigned business version of the Composition (analogous to CDA ClinicalDocument.versionNumber). It is distinct from Resource.meta.versionId, which is a server-assigned technical version that every resource carries and that may change whenever the resource is updated on a server. Composition.version reflects the version of a logical document's content and remains constant even if the Composition or its referenced resources are moved between servers and receive new meta.versionId values.

element.short: Represents informed consents and medico-legal transactions
element.definition: References the consents associated with this document. Examples include a consent to perform the clinical service being documented (.event) or a consent for the information contained in the document to be released to a third party.
A plan, proposal or order that is fulfilled in whole or in part by this composition.
element.requirements: Allows tracing of authorization for the event and tracking whether proposals/recommendations were acted upon.

element.short: registered | partial | preliminary | final | amended | corrected | appended | cancelled | entered-in-error | deprecated | unknown
element.definition: The workflow/clinical status of this composition. The status is a marker for the clinical standing of the document.
element.comment: See section 2.8.3.2, The workflow/clinical status of the composition, for guidance.  Because the entered-in-error flag changes how this resource and its related elements must be interpreted, status is labeled as a modifier element. Some reporting workflows require that the original narrative of a final document never be altered; instead, only new narrative can be added. The Composition resource has no explicit status for noting whether this business rule is in effect; this would be handled by an extension if required.
element.requirements: Need to be able to mark interim, amended, or withdrawn compositions or documents.
element.isModifierReason: This element is labelled as a modifier because it is a status element that contains status entered-in-error which means that the resource should not be treated as valid

binding.description: The workflow status of the composition.

element.comment: For Composition type, LOINC is ubiquitous and strongly endorsed by HL7. Most implementation guides will require a specific LOINC code, or use LOINC as an extensible binding.
element.requirements: Key metadata element describing the composition, used in searching/filtering.

binding.description: Type of a composition.

element.definition: A categorization for the type of the composition - helps with indexing and searching. This may be implied by or derived from the code specified in the Composition Type.
element.requirements: Helps humans to assess whether the composition is of interest when viewing an index of compositions or documents.

binding.description: High-level kind of a clinical document at a macro level.

element.short: Who and/or what the composition is about
element.definition: Who or what the composition is about. The composition can be about a person, (patient or healthcare practitioner), a device (e.g. a machine) or even a group of subjects (such as a document about a herd of livestock, or a set of patients that share a common exposure).
element.comment: For clinical documents, this is usually the patient.
element.requirements: Essential metadata for searching for the composition. Identifies who and/or what the composition/document is about.

element.definition: Describes the clinical encounter or type of care this documentation is associated with.
element.requirements: Provides context for the composition and supports searching.

element.definition: The composition editing time, when the composition was last logically changed by the author.
element.comment: The Last Modified Date on the composition may be after the date the document was attested without being changed. This means that the date on an amended document is the date of the amendment, not the date of original authorship.
element.requirements: dateTime is used for tracking, organizing versions and searching. Note that this is the time of authoring this version of the Composition. When packaged in a document, [Bundle.timestamp](bundle-definitions.html#Bundle.timestamp) is the date of packaging.

element.comment: When multiple useContexts are specified, there is no expectation that all or any of the contexts apply.
element.requirements: Assist in searching for appropriate content.

element.comment: When the Composition is software-generated, a Device can be referenced. When a software-generated Composition is verified by a human (but not authored by that human), use the attester element to identify the human(s) who performed the verification.
element.requirements: Identifies who is responsible for the content.

element.short: Identifies supporting entities, including parents, relatives, caregivers, insurance policyholders, guarantors, and others related in some way to the patient
element.definition: Identifies supporting entities, including parents, relatives, caregivers, insurance policyholders, guarantors, and others related in some way to the patient. A supporting person or organization is an individual or an organization with a relationship to the patient. A supporting person who is playing multiple roles would be recorded in multiple participants (e.g., emergency contact and next-of-kin).

element.definition: Meaning and purpose of participation, in creation of the clinical document. The list includes: data entry person, informant, primary information recipient, and tracker. Other types are allowed.

resource.name: ConceptMap
resource.description: A statement of relationships from one set of concepts to one or more other concepts - either concepts in code systems, or data element/data element concepts, or classes in class models.

element.short: A map from one set of concepts to one or more other concepts
element.definition: A statement of relationships from one set of concepts to one or more other concepts - either concepts in code systems, or data element/data element concepts, or classes in class models.

constraint.human: Name should be usable as an identifier for the module by machine processing applications such as code generation

element.definition: The logical id of the resource, as used in the URL for the resource. Once assigned, this value never changes.
element.comment: Within the context of the FHIR RESTful interactions, the resource has an id except for cases like the create and conditional update. Otherwise, the use of the resource id depends on the given use case.

element.definition: The metadata about the resource. This is content that is maintained by the infrastructure. Changes to the content might not always be associated with version changes to the resource.

constraint.human: All FHIR elements must have a @value or children

element.short: A set of rules under which this content was created
element.definition: A reference to a set of rules that were followed when the resource was constructed, and which must be understood when processing the content. Often, this is a reference to an implementation guide that defines the special rules along with other profiles etc. For DomainResources, if more than one implicitRules policy applies, additional policies may be conveyed using the [additionalImplicitRules](https://build.fhir.org/ig/HL7/fhir-extensions/StructureDefinition-additionalImplicitRules.html) extension.
element.comment: Asserting this rule set restricts the content to be only understood by a limited set of trading partners. This inherently limits the usefulness of the data in the long term. However, the existing health eco-system is highly fractured, and not yet ready to define, collect, and exchange data in a generally computable sense. Wherever possible, implementers and/or specification writers should avoid using this element. Often, when used, the URL is a reference to an implementation guide that defines these special rules as part of its narrative along with other profiles, value sets, etc.

constraint.human: All FHIR elements must have a @value or children

element.isModifierReason: This element is labeled as a modifier because the implicit rules may provide additional knowledge about the resource that modifies its meaning or interpretation

element.definition: The base language in which the resource is written.
element.comment: Language is provided to support indexing and accessibility (typically, services such as text to speech use the language tag). The html language tag in the narrative applies  to the narrative. The language tag on the resource may be used to specify the language of other presentations generated from the data in the resource. Not all the content has to be in the base language. The Resource.language should not be assumed to apply to the narrative automatically. If a language is specified, it should it also be specified on the div element in the html (see rules in HTML5 for information about the relationship between xml:lang and the html lang attribute).

constraint.human: All FHIR elements must have a @value or children
