element.definition: Specific type of encounter (e.g. e-mail consultation, surgical day-care, skilled nursing, rehabilitation).
element.comment: Since there are many ways to further classify encounters, this element is 0..*.

extension.valueMarkdown: The type of encounter.

binding.description: A specific code indicating type of service provided

element.short: The specific service that is to be performed during this encounter
element.definition: The specific service that is to be performed during this encounter.

binding.description: Broad categorization of the service that is to be provided.

element.short: The patient or group related to this encounter
element.definition: The patient or group related to this encounter. In some use-cases the patient MAY not be present, such as a case meeting about a patient between several practitioners or a careteam.
element.comment: While the encounter is always about the patient, the patient might not actually be known in all contexts of use, and there may be a group of patients that could be anonymous (such as in a group therapy for Alcoholics Anonymous - where the recording of the encounter could be used for billing on the number of people/staff and not important to the context of the specific patients) or alternately in veterinary care a herd of sheep receiving treatment (where the animals are not individually tracked).

element.short: The current status of the subject in relation to the Encounter
element.definition: The subjectStatus value can be used to track the patient's status within the encounter. It details whether the patient has arrived or departed, has been triaged or is currently in a waiting status.
element.comment: Different use-cases are likely to have different permitted transitions between states, such as an Emergency department could use `arrived` when the patient first presents, then `triaged` once has been assessed by a nurse, then `receiving-care` once treatment begins, however other sectors may use a different set of these values, or their own custom set in place of this example valueset provided.

binding.description: Current status of the subject  within the encounter.

element.short: Episode(s) of care that this encounter should be recorded against
element.definition: Where a specific encounter should be classified as a part of a specific episode(s) of care this field should be used. This association can facilitate grouping of related encounters together for a specific purpose, such as government reporting, issue tracking, association via a common problem.  The association is recorded on the encounter as these are typically created after the episode of care and grouped on entry rather than editing the episode of care to append another encounter to it (the episode of care could span years).

element.short: The request that initiated this encounter
element.definition: The request this encounter satisfies (e.g. incoming referral or procedure request).

element.short: The group(s) that are allocated to participate in this encounter
element.definition: The group(s) of individuals, organizations that are allocated to participate in this encounter. The participants backbone will record the actuals of when these individuals participated during the encounter.

element.short: Another Encounter this encounter is part of
element.definition: Another Encounter of which this encounter is a part of (administratively or in time).
element.comment: This is also used for associating a child's encounter back to the mother's encounter.Refer to the Notes section in the Patient resource for further details.

element.short: The organization (facility) responsible for this encounter
element.definition: The organization that is primarily responsible for this Encounter's services. This MAY be the same as the organization on the Patient record, however it could be different, such as if the actor performing the services was from an external organization (which may be billed seperately) for an external consultation.  Refer to the colonoscopy example on the Encounter examples tab.

element.short: List of participants involved in the encounter
element.definition: The list of people responsible for providing the service.
element.comment: Any Patient or Group present in the participation.actor must also be the subject, though the subject may be absent from the participation.actor for cases where the patient (or group) is not present, such as during a case review conference.

constraint.human: A type must be provided when no explicit actor is specified
A type cannot be provided for a patient or group participant
constraint.expression: actor.exists(resolve() is Patient or resolve() is Group) implies type.exists().not()

element.definition: Role of participant in encounter.
element.comment: The participant type indicates how an individual actor participates in an encounter. It includes non-practitioner participants, and for practitioners this is to describe the action type in the context of this encounter (e.g. Admitting Dr, Attending Dr, Translator, Consulting Dr). This is different to the practitioner roles which are functional roles, derived from terms of employment, education, licensing, etc. Patient and Groups are not permitted to have types as they are the subject of the encounter (invariant enc-2 enforces this).

binding.description: Role of participant in encounter.

element.short: Period of time during the encounter that the participant participated
element.definition: The period of time that the specified participant participated in the encounter. These can overlap or be sub-sets of the overall encounter's period.
element.comment: This can overlap or be sub-sets of the overall encounter's period as noted in Encounter.actualPeriod.

element.short: The individual, device, or service participating in the encounter
element.definition: Person involved in the encounter, the patient/group is also included here to indicate that the patient was actually participating in the encounter. Not including the patient here covers use cases such as a case meeting between practitioners about a patient - non contact times.
element.comment: For planning purposes, Appointments may include a CareTeam participant to indicate that one specific person from the CareTeam will be assigned, but that assignment might not happen until the Encounter begins. Hence CareTeam is not included in Encounter.participant, as the specific individual should be assigned and represented as a Practitioner or other person resource.Similarly, Location can be included in Appointment.participant to assist with planning.  However, the patient location is tracked on the Encounter in the Encounter.location property to allow for additional metadata and history to be recorded.The role of the participant can be used to declare what the actor will be doing in the scope of this encounter participation.If the individual is not specified during planning, then it is expected that the individual will be filled in at a later stage prior to the encounter commencing.

element.short: The appointment that scheduled this encounter
element.definition: The appointment that scheduled this encounter.

element.short: Connection details of a virtual service (e.g. conference call)
element.definition: Connection details of a virtual service (e.g. conference call).
element.comment: There are two types of virtual meetings that often exist:* a persistent, virtual meeting room that can only be used for a single purpose at a time, * and a dynamic virtual meeting room that is generated on demand for a specific purpose.Implementers may consider using Location.virtualService for persistent meeting rooms.If each participant would have a different meeting link, an extension using the VirtualServiceContactDetail  can be applied to the Encounter.participant BackboneElement.

element.short: The actual start and end time of the encounter
element.definition: The actual start and end time of the encounter.
element.comment: If not (yet) known, the end of the Period may be omitted. Not all participants/locations in the encounter need to occur within the period defined in actualPeriod. For example, a common use case is actors associated with preparations/cleanup for the encounter.

element.short: The planned start date/time (or admission date) of the encounter
element.definition: The planned start date/time (or admission date) of the encounter.

element.short: The planned end date/time (or discharge date) of the encounter
element.definition: The planned end date/time (or discharge date) of the encounter.

element.short: Actual quantity of time the encounter lasted (less time absent)
element.definition: Actual quantity of time the encounter lasted. This excludes the time during leaves of absence.When missing it is the time in between the start and end values.
element.comment: If the precision on these values is low (e.g. to the day only) then this may be considered was an all day (or multi-day) encounter, unless the duration is included, where that amount of time occurred sometime during the interval.May differ from the time in `Encounter.period` due to leave of absence(s).

mapping.map: (PV1-45 less PV1-44) iff ( (PV1-44 not empty) and (PV1-45 not empty) ); units in minutes or PV2-11 (which is actual length in days)

element.short: The list of medical reasons that are expected to be addressed during the encounter
element.definition: The list of medical reasons that are expected to be addressed during the encounter.
element.comment: The reason communicates what medical problem the patient has that should be addressed during the encounter.  This reason could be patient reported complaint, a clinical indication that was determined in a previous encounter or episode of care, or some planned care such as an immunization recommendation.  In the case where you have a primary reason, but are expecting to also address other problems, you can list the primary reason with a use code of 'Chief Complaint', while the other problems being addressed would have a use code of 'Reason for Visit'.Examples: * pregnancy would use HealthcareService or a coding as the reason * patient home monitoring could use Condition as the reason

element.short: What the reason value should be used for/as
element.definition: What the reason value should be used as e.g. Chief Complaint, Health Concern, Health Maintenance (including screening).

element.short: Reason the encounter takes place (core or reference)
element.definition: Reason the encounter takes place, expressed as a code or a reference to another resource. For admissions, this can be used for a coded admission diagnosis.

binding.description: Reason why the encounter takes place.

mapping.map: EVN-4 / PV2-3 (note: PV2-3 is nominally constrained to inpatient admissions; HL7 V2 makes no vocabulary suggestions for PV2-3; would not expect PV2 segment or PV2-3 to be in use in all implementations )

element.short: The list of diagnosis relevant to this encounter
element.definition: The list of diagnosis relevant to this encounter.
element.comment: Also note that for the purpose of billing, the diagnoses are recorded in the account where they can be ranked appropriately for how the invoicing/claiming documentation needs to be prepared.

element.short: The diagnosis relevant to the encounter
element.definition: The coded diagnosis or a reference to a Condition (with other resources referenced in the evidence.detail), the use property will indicate the purpose of this specific diagnosis.

mapping.map: Resources that would commonly referenced at Encounter.indication would be Condition and/or Procedure. These most closely align with DG1/PRB and PR1 respectively.

element.short: Role that this diagnosis has within the encounter (e.g. admission, billing, discharge …)
element.definition: Role that this diagnosis has within the encounter (e.g. admission, billing, discharge …).

binding.description: The type of diagnosis this condition represents.

element.short: The set of accounts that may be used for billing for this Encounter
element.definition: The set of accounts that may be used for billing for this Encounter.
element.comment: The billing system may choose to allocate billable items associated with the Encounter to different referenced Accounts based on internal business rules.Also note that the Encounter.account properties are meant to represent long-running or perpetual accounts.  For short-lived, episodic accounts, see Account.covers.

element.short: Diet preferences reported by the patient
element.definition: Diet preferences reported by the patient.
element.comment: For example, a patient may request both a dairy-free and nut-free diet preference (not mutually exclusive).
element.requirements: Used to track patient's diet restrictions and/or preference. For a complete description of the nutrition needs of a patient during their stay, one should use the nutritionOrder resource which links to Encounter.

binding.description: Medical, cultural or ethical food preferences to help with catering requirements.

element.definition: Any special requests that have been made for this encounter, such as the provision of specific equipment or other things.

binding.description: Special arrangements.

element.definition: Special courtesies that may be provided to the patient during the encounter (VIP, board member, professional courtesy).
element.comment: Although the specialCourtesy property can contain values like VIP, the purpose of this field is intended to be used for flagging additional `benefits` that might occur for the patient during the encounter.It could include things like the patient is to have a private room, special room features, receive a friendly visit from hospital adminisitration, or should be briefed on treatment by senior staff during the stay.It is not specifically intended to be used for securing the specific record - that is the purpose of the security meta tag, and where appropriate, both fields could be used.

binding.description: Special courtesies.

element.short: Details about the admission to a healthcare service
element.definition: Details about the stay during which a healthcare service is provided.This does not describe the event of admitting the patient, but rather any information that is relevant from the time of admittance until the time of discharge.
element.comment: An Encounter may cover more than just the inpatient stay. Contexts such as outpatients, community clinics, and aged care facilities are also included.The duration recorded in the period of this encounter covers the entire scope of this admission record.

element.definition: Pre-admission identifier.

element.short: The location/organization from which the patient came before admission
element.definition: The location/organization from which the patient came before admission.

element.short: From where patient was admitted (physician referral, transfer)
element.definition: From where patient was admitted (physician referral, transfer).

binding.description: From where the patient was admitted.

element.short: Indicates that the patient is being re-admitted
element.definition: Indicates that this encounter is directly related to a prior admission, often because the conditions addressed in the prior admission were not fully addressed.

binding.description: The reason for re-admission of this admission encounter.

element.short: Location/organization to which the patient is discharged
element.definition: Location/organization to which the patient is discharged.

element.short: Category or kind of location after discharge
element.definition: Category or kind of location after discharge.

binding.description: Discharge Disposition.

element.short: List of locations where the patient has been
element.definition: List of locations where  the patient has been during this encounter.
element.comment: Virtual encounters can be recorded in the Encounter by specifying a location reference to a location of type "kind" such as "client's home" and an encounter.class = "virtual".

element.definition: The location where the encounter takes place.
The status of the participants' presence at the specified location during the period specified. If the participant is no longer at the location, then the period will have an end date/time.
element.comment: When the patient is no longer active at a location, then the period end date is entered, and the status may be changed to completed.

binding.description: The status of the location.

element.short: The form of the location (usually the level in the location hierarchy - bed, room, ward, virtual etc.)
element.definition: This will be used to specify the required levels (bed/ward/room/etc.) desired to be recorded to simplify either messaging or query.
element.comment:
This information is de-normalized from the Location resource to support the easier understanding of the encounter resource and processing in messaging or query.

There may be many levels in the hierachy, and this may only pic specific levels that are required for a specific usage scenario.

binding.description: Form of the location.

element.short: Time period during which the patient was present at the location
element.definition: Time period during which the patient was present at the location.
element.comment: This can overlap or be sub-sets of the overall encounter's period as noted in Encounter.actualPeriod.

resource.name: Endpoint
resource.description: The technical details of an endpoint that can be used for electronic services, such as for web services providing XDS.b, a REST endpoint for another FHIR server, or a s/Mime email address. This may include any security context information.

element.short: The technical details of an endpoint that can be used for electronic services
element.definition: The technical details of an endpoint that can be used for electronic services, such as for web services providing XDS.b, a REST endpoint for another FHIR server, or a s/Mime email address. This may include any security context information.

constraint.human: If the resource is contained in another resource, it SHALL NOT contain nested Resources
If the resource is contained in another resource, it SHALL be referred to from elsewhere in the resource or SHALL refer to the containing resource
constraint.expression: contained.where((('#'+id.trace('id') in %resource.descendants().select(reference | as(uri))) or descendants().where(reference='#' | as(uri)='#').exists()).not()).trace('unmatched', id).empty()

constraint.human: If a resource is contained in another resource, it SHALL NOT have a meta.versionId or a meta.lastUpdated
If a resource is contained in another resource, it SHALL NOT have a security label

extension.valueMarkdown: When a resource has no narrative, only systems that fully understand the data can display the resource to a human safely. Including a human readable representation in the resource makes for a much more robust ecosystem and cheaper handling of resources by intermediary systems. Some ecosystems restrict distribution of resources to only those systems that do fully understand the resources, and as a consequence implementers may believe that the narrative is superfluous. However experience shows that such ecosystems often open up to new participants over time.

constraint.human: A resource should have narrative for robust management

element.definition: The logical id of the resource, as used in the URL for the resource. Once assigned, this value never changes.
element.comment: Within the context of the FHIR RESTful interactions, the resource has an id except for cases like the create and conditional update. Otherwise, the use of the resource id depends on the given use case.

element.definition: The metadata about the resource. This is content that is maintained by the infrastructure. Changes to the content might not always be associated with version changes to the resource.

constraint.human: All FHIR elements must have a @value or children

element.short: A set of rules under which this content was created
element.definition: A reference to a set of rules that were followed when the resource was constructed, and which must be understood when processing the content. Often, this is a reference to an implementation guide that defines the special rules along with other profiles etc. For DomainResources, if more than one implicitRules policy applies, additional policies may be conveyed using the [additionalImplicitRules](https://build.fhir.org/ig/HL7/fhir-extensions/StructureDefinition-additionalImplicitRules.html) extension.
element.comment: Asserting this rule set restricts the content to be only understood by a limited set of trading partners. This inherently limits the usefulness of the data in the long term. However, the existing health eco-system is highly fractured, and not yet ready to define, collect, and exchange data in a generally computable sense. Wherever possible, implementers and/or specification writers should avoid using this element. Often, when used, the URL is a reference to an implementation guide that defines these special rules as part of its narrative along with other profiles, value sets, etc.

constraint.human: All FHIR elements must have a @value or children

element.isModifierReason: This element is labeled as a modifier because the implicit rules may provide additional knowledge about the resource that modifies its meaning or interpretation

element.definition: The base language in which the resource is written.
element.comment: Language is provided to support indexing and accessibility (typically, services such as text to speech use the language tag). The html language tag in the narrative applies  to the narrative. The language tag on the resource may be used to specify the language of other presentations generated from the data in the resource. Not all the content has to be in the base language. The Resource.language should not be assumed to apply to the narrative automatically. If a language is specified, it should it also be specified on the div element in the html (see rules in HTML5 for information about the relationship between xml:lang and the html lang attribute).

constraint.human: All FHIR elements must have a @value or children

binding.description: IETF language tag for a human language

element.short: Text summary of the resource, for human interpretation
element.definition: A human-readable narrative that contains a summary of the resource and can be used to represent the content of the resource to a human. The narrative need not encode all the structured data, but is required to contain sufficient detail to make it "clinically safe" for a human to just read the narrative. Resource definitions may define what content should be represented in the narrative to ensure clinical safety.
element.comment: Contained resources do not have a narrative. Resources that are not contained SHOULD have a narrative. In some cases, a resource may only have text with little or no additional discrete data (as long as all minOccurs=1 elements are satisfied).  This may be necessary for data from legacy systems where information is captured as a "text blob" or where text is additionally entered raw or narrated and encoded information is added later.

constraint.human: All FHIR elements must have a @value or children

element.definition: These resources do not have an independent existence apart from the resource that contains them - they cannot be identified independently, nor can they have their own independent transaction scope. This is allowed to be a Parameters resource if and only if it is referenced by a resource that provides context/meaning.
element.comment: This should never be done when the content can be identified properly, as once identification is lost, it is extremely difficult (and context dependent) to restore it again. Contained resources may have profiles and tags in their meta elements, but SHALL NOT have security labels. Contained resources may be a resource type defined in the FHIR specification, or an [additional resource](resource.html#additional).

element.definition: The endpoint status represents whether the endpoint can currently be used for connections or why it can't be used.

element.comment: For additional connectivity details for the protocol, extensions will be used at this point, as in the XDS example. If there are multiple payload types or mimetypes they are all applicable for all connection types, and all have the same status.

constraint.human: All FHIR elements must have a @value or children

element.short: The type of environment(s) exposed at this endpoint
element.definition: The type of environment(s) exposed at this endpoint (dev, prod, test, etc.).

constraint.human: All FHIR elements must have a @value or children

element.short: Organization that manages this endpoint (might not be the organization that exposes the endpoint)
element.definition: The organization that provides technical management services for this endpoint.  This would be the organization that acts as the public help desk for when the endpoint is not functioning.  It does NOT necessarily represent the organization who is the steward of data being provided/accepted by the endpoint.
element.comment: This property would NOT be used if the organization is only providing technical infrastructure.  For example, it would NOT refer to the cloud hosting provider if that provider were not providing helpdesk support for the endpoint.This property would NOT be used to represent the entity that is the steward of the data exposed by the endpoint.  This should be represented via Organization.endpoint. PractitionerRole.endpoint, Location.endpoint, or the other directory resources that may refer to endpoints.This property is not typically used when searching for Endpoint resources for the purpose of retrieving or sending clinical or administrative data.  However you may use this property to find endpoints for other technical administrative reasons such as if an organization that is managing endpoints is going out of business, you may need to update to the new managing organization.

element.definition: Contact details for a human to contact about the endpoint. The primary use of this for system administrator troubleshooting.

element.comment: Temporary downtimes or other short-term changes in availability would not be represented in this property.

element.short: Times the endpoint is expected to be available (including exceptions)
element.definition: The times the endpoint is expected to be available, including transient downtimes and any exceptions.
element.comment: Endpoint.availability is meant to represent specific availability, including temporary downtimes or other short term changes in availability.  Conversely, Endpoint.period is meant to represent the general **planned** period of time when the Endpoint may be used, for example when an endpoint is being commissioned or decommissioned.  For example, if an Endpoint is only available during business hours (9-5), the lack of availability during the night would not be reflected in Endpoint.period,but would be reflected in Endpoint.availability.

resource.name: EventDefinition
resource.description: The EventDefinition resource provides a reusable description of when a particular event can occur.

element.short: A description of when an event can occur
element.definition: The EventDefinition resource provides a reusable description of when a particular event can occur.

constraint.human: Name should be usable as an identifier for the module by machine processing applications such as code generation

element.definition: The logical id of the resource, as used in the URL for the resource. Once assigned, this value never changes.
element.comment: Within the context of the FHIR RESTful interactions, the resource has an id except for cases like the create and conditional update. Otherwise, the use of the resource id depends on the given use case.

element.definition: The metadata about the resource. This is content that is maintained by the infrastructure. Changes to the content might not always be associated with version changes to the resource.

constraint.human: All FHIR elements must have a @value or children

element.short: A set of rules under which this content was created
element.definition: A reference to a set of rules that were followed when the resource was constructed, and which must be understood when processing the content. Often, this is a reference to an implementation guide that defines the special rules along with other profiles etc. For DomainResources, if more than one implicitRules policy applies, additional policies may be conveyed using the [additionalImplicitRules](https://build.fhir.org/ig/HL7/fhir-extensions/StructureDefinition-additionalImplicitRules.html) extension.
element.comment: Asserting this rule set restricts the content to be only understood by a limited set of trading partners. This inherently limits the usefulness of the data in the long term. However, the existing health eco-system is highly fractured, and not yet ready to define, collect, and exchange data in a generally computable sense. Wherever possible, implementers and/or specification writers should avoid using this element. Often, when used, the URL is a reference to an implementation guide that defines these special rules as part of its narrative along with other profiles, value sets, etc.

constraint.human: All FHIR elements must have a @value or children

element.isModifierReason: This element is labeled as a modifier because the implicit rules may provide additional knowledge about the resource that modifies its meaning or interpretation

element.definition: The base language in which the resource is written.
element.comment: Language is provided to support indexing and accessibility (typically, services such as text to speech use the language tag). The html language tag in the narrative applies  to the narrative. The language tag on the resource may be used to specify the language of other presentations generated from the data in the resource. Not all the content has to be in the base language. The Resource.language should not be assumed to apply to the narrative automatically. If a language is specified, it should it also be specified on the div element in the html (see rules in HTML5 for information about the relationship between xml:lang and the html lang attribute).

constraint.human: All FHIR elements must have a @value or children

binding.description: IETF language tag for a human language

element.short: Text summary of the resource, for human interpretation
element.definition: A human-readable narrative that contains a summary of the resource and can be used to represent the content of the resource to a human. The narrative need not encode all the structured data, but is required to contain sufficient detail to make it "clinically safe" for a human to just read the narrative. Resource definitions may define what content should be represented in the narrative to ensure clinical safety.
element.comment: Contained resources do not have a narrative. Resources that are not contained SHOULD have a narrative. In some cases, a resource may only have text with little or no additional discrete data (as long as all minOccurs=1 elements are satisfied).  This may be necessary for data from legacy systems where information is captured as a "text blob" or where text is additionally entered raw or narrated and encoded information is added later.

constraint.human: All FHIR elements must have a @value or children

element.definition: These resources do not have an independent existence apart from the resource that contains them - they cannot be identified independently, nor can they have their own independent transaction scope. This is allowed to be a Parameters resource if and only if it is referenced by a resource that provides context/meaning.
element.comment: This should never be done when the content can be identified properly, as once identification is lost, it is extremely difficult (and context dependent) to restore it again. Contained resources may have profiles and tags in their meta elements, but SHALL NOT have security labels. Contained resources may be a resource type defined in the FHIR specification, or an [additional resource](resource.html#additional).

slicing.description: Extensions are always sliced by (at least) url

element.definition: May be used to represent additional information that is not part of the basic definition of the resource. To make the use of extensions safe and managable, there is a strict set of governance applied to the definition and use of extensions. Though any implementer can define an extension, there is a set of requirements that SHALL be met as part of the definition of the extension.
element.comment: There can be no stigma associated with the use of extensions by any application, project, or standard - regardless of the institution or jurisdiction that uses or defines the extensions.  The use of extensions is what allows the FHIR specification to retain a core level of simplicity for everyone.

constraint.human: All FHIR elements must have a @value or children

slicing.description: Extensions are always sliced by (at least) url

element.definition:
May be used to represent additional information that is not part of the basic definition of the resource and that modifies the understanding of the element that contains it and/or the understanding of the containing element's descendants. Usually modifier elements provide negation or qualification. To make the use of extensions safe and managable, there is a strict set of governance applied to the definition and use of extensions. Though any implementer is allowed to define an extension, there is a set of requirements that SHALL be met as part of the definition of the extension. Applications processing a resource are required to check for modifier extensions.

Modifier extensions SHALL NOT change the meaning of any elements on Resource or DomainResource (including cannot change the meaning of modifierExtension itself).
element.comment: There can be no stigma associated with the use of extensions by any application, project, or standard - regardless of the institution or jurisdiction that uses or defines the extensions.  The use of extensions is what allows the FHIR specification to retain a core level of simplicity for everyone.
element.requirements: Modifier extensions allow for extensions that *cannot* be safely ignored to be clearly distinguished from the vast majority of extensions which can be safely ignored.  This promotes interoperability by eliminating the need for implementers to prohibit the presence of extensions. For further information, see the [definition of modifier extensions](extensibility.html#modifierExtension).

constraint.human: All FHIR elements must have a @value or children

element.isModifierReason: Modifier extensions are expected to modify the meaning or interpretation of the resource that contains them

element.short: Canonical identifier for this event definition, represented as a URI (globally unique)
element.definition: An absolute URI that is used to identify this event definition when it is referenced in a specification, model, design or an instance; also called its canonical identifier. This SHOULD be globally unique and SHOULD be a literal address at which an authoritative instance of this event definition is (or will be) published. This URL can be the target of a canonical reference. It SHALL remain the same when the event definition is stored on different servers.
element.comment:
Can be a urn:uuid: or a urn:oid: but real http: addresses are preferred.  Multiple instances may share the same URL if they have a distinct version.

The determination of when to create a new version of a resource (same url, new version) vs. defining a new artifact is up to the author.  Considerations for making this decision are found in [Technical and Business Versions](resource.html#versions). 

In some cases, the resource can no longer be found at the stated url, but the url itself cannot change. Implementations can use the [meta.source](resource.html#meta) element to indicate where the current master source of the resource can be found.
element.requirements: Allows the event definition to be referenced by a single globally unique identifier.

constraint.human: URL should not contain | or # - these characters make processing canonical references problematic
All FHIR elements must have a @value or children

element.short: Additional identifier for the event definition
element.definition: A formal identifier that is used to identify this event definition when it is represented in other formats, or referenced in a specification, model, design or an instance.
element.requirements: Allows externally provided and/or usable business identifiers to be easily associated with the module.

constraint.human: All FHIR elements must have a @value or children

element.short: Business version of the event definition
element.definition: The identifier that is used to identify this version of the event definition when it is referenced in a specification, model, design or instance. This is an arbitrary value managed by the event definition author and is not expected to be globally unique. For example, it might be a timestamp (e.g. yyyymmdd) if a managed version is not available. There is also no expectation that versions can be placed in a lexicographical sequence. For more information on versioning knowledge artifacts, refer to the Canonical Resource Management Infrastructure (CRMI) implementation guide artifact versioning discussion (http://hl7.org/fhir/uv/crmi/artifact-lifecycle.html#artifact-versioning).
element.comment: There may be different event definition instances that have the same identifier but different versions.  The version can be appended to the url in a reference to allow a reference to a particular business version of the event definition with the format [url]|[version]. The version SHOULD NOT contain a '#' - see [Business Version](resource.html#bv-format).

constraint.human: All FHIR elements must have a @value or children

element.definition: Indicates the mechanism used to compare versions to determine which is more current.
element.comment: If set as a string, this is a FHIRPath expression that has two additional context variables passed in - %version1 and %version2 and will return a negative number if version1 is newer, a positive number if version2 and a 0 if the version ordering can't be successfully be determined.

constraint.human: All FHIR elements must have a @value or children

element.short: Name for this event definition (computer friendly)
element.definition: A natural language name identifying the event definition. This name should be usable as an identifier for the module by machine processing applications such as code generation.
element.comment: The name is not expected to be globally unique. The name should be a simple alphanumeric type name to ensure that it is machine-processing friendly.
element.requirements: Support human navigation and code generation.

constraint.human: All FHIR elements must have a @value or children

element.short: Name for this event definition (human friendly)
element.definition: A short, descriptive, user-friendly title for the event definition.
element.comment: This name does not need to be machine-processing friendly and may contain punctuation, white-space, etc.

constraint.human: All FHIR elements must have a @value or children

element.short: Subordinate title of the event definition
element.definition: An explanatory or alternate title for the event definition giving additional information about its content.

constraint.human: All FHIR elements must have a @value or children

element.definition: The status of this event definition. Enables tracking the life-cycle of the content.
element.comment:
Allows filtering of event definitions that are appropriate for use versus not.

See guidance around (not) making local changes to elements [here](canonicalresource.html#localization).

constraint.human: All FHIR elements must have a @value or children

element.isModifierReason: This is labeled as "Is Modifier" because applications should not use a retired {{title}} without due consideration

binding.description: The lifecycle status of an artifact.

element.short: For testing only - never for real usage
element.definition: A Boolean value to indicate that this event definition is authored for testing purposes (or education/evaluation/marketing) and no version of this resource will ever be intended for genuine usage.
element.comment:
Allows filtering of event definitions that are appropriate for use versus not. Experimental resources might include example instances in implementation guides, instances created solely for testing purposes, etc. If experimental is 'true' for any version of a resource, it should be true for all versions of the resource.  (If experimental changes, then it is being misused or a resource that was never intended for real-world use has unexpectedly changed its purpose.).

Experimental resources are not expected to be stable and may well have breaking changes without a corresponding change to the 'version' element.
element.requirements: Enables experimental content to be developed following the same lifecycle that would be used for a production-level event definition.
element.meaningWhenMissing: If absent, this resource is treated as though it is not experimental.

constraint.human: All FHIR elements must have a @value or children

element.short: Type of individual the event definition is focused on
element.definition: A code or group definition that describes the intended subject of the event definition.
element.meaningWhenMissing: Patient

constraint.human: All FHIR elements must have a @value or children

binding.description: The possible types of subjects for an event (E.g. Patient, Practitioner, Organization, Location, etc.).

element.definition: The date  (and optionally time) when the event definition was last significantly changed. The date must change when the business version changes and it must change if the status code changes. In addition, it should change when the substantive content of the event definition changes.
element.comment:
The date is often not tracked until the resource is published, but may be present on draft content. Note that this is not the same as the resource last-modified-date, since the resource may be a secondary representation of the event definition. Additional specific dates may be added as extensions or be found by consulting Provenances associated with past versions of the resource.

See guidance around (not) making local changes to elements [here](canonicalresource.html#localization).

constraint.human: All FHIR elements must have a @value or children

element.short: Name of the publisher/steward (organization or individual)
element.definition: The name of the organization or individual responsible for the release and ongoing maintenance of the event definition.
element.comment: Usually an organization but may be an individual. The publisher (or steward) of the event definition is the organization or individual primarily responsible for the maintenance and upkeep of the event definition. This is not necessarily the same individual or organization that developed and initially authored the content. The publisher is the primary point of contact for questions or issues with the event definition. This item SHOULD be populated unless the information is available from context.
element.requirements: Helps establish the "authority/credibility" of the event definition.  May also allow for contact.

constraint.human: All FHIR elements must have a @value or children

element.definition: Contact details to assist a user in finding and communicating with the publisher.
element.comment:
May be a web site, an email address, a telephone number, etc.

See guidance around (not) making local changes to elements [here](canonicalresource.html#localization).

constraint.human: All FHIR elements must have a @value or children

element.short: Natural language description of the event definition
element.definition: A free text natural language description of the event definition from a consumer's perspective.
element.comment: This description can be used to capture details such as comments about misuse, instructions for clinical use and interpretation, literature references, examples from the paper world, etc. It is not a rendering of the event definition as conveyed in the 'text' field of the resource itself. This item SHOULD be populated unless the information is available from context (e.g. the language of the event definition is presumed to be the predominant language in the place the event definition was created).

constraint.human: All FHIR elements must have a @value or children

element.short: The context that the content is intended to support
element.definition: The content was developed with a focus and intent of supporting the contexts that are listed. These contexts may be general categories (gender, age, ...) or may be references to specific programs (insurance plans, studies, ...) and may be used to assist with indexing and searching for appropriate event definition instances.
element.comment: When multiple useContexts are specified, there is no expectation that all or any of the contexts apply.
element.requirements: Assist in searching for appropriate content.

constraint.human: All FHIR elements must have a @value or children

element.short: Jurisdiction of the authority that maintains the event definition (if applicable)
element.definition: A legal or geographic region in which the authority that maintains the resource is operating.  In general, the jurisdiction is also found in the useContext.  The useContext may reference additional jurisdictions because the defining jurisdiction does not necessarily limit the jurisdictions of use.
element.comment: It may be possible for the event definition to be used in jurisdictions other than those for which it was originally designed or intended.

constraint.human: All FHIR elements must have a @value or children

binding.description: Countries and regions within which this artifact is targeted for use.

element.short: Why this event definition is defined
element.definition: Explanation of why this event definition is needed and why it has been designed as it has.
element.comment: This element does not describe the usage of the event definition. Instead, it provides traceability of ''why'' the resource is either needed or ''why'' it is defined as it is.  This may be used to point to source materials or specifications that drove the structure of this event definition.

constraint.human: All FHIR elements must have a @value or children

element.short: Describes the clinical usage of the event definition
element.definition: A detailed description of how the event definition is used from a clinical perspective.

constraint.human: All FHIR elements must have a @value or children

element.short: Notice about intellectual property ownership, can include restrictions on use
element.definition: A copyright statement relating to the event definition and/or its contents. Copyright statements are notices of intellectual property ownership and can include restrictions on the use and publishing of the event definition.
element.comment: The short copyright declaration (e.g. (c) '2015+ xyz organization') should be sent in the copyrightLabel element without the copyright prefix (i.e., do not include '(c)' or the symbol).
element.requirements: Consumers must be able to determine any legal restrictions on the use of the event definition and/or its content.

constraint.human: All FHIR elements must have a @value or children

element.definition: A short string (<50 characters), suitable for inclusion in a page footer that identifies the copyright holder, effective period, and optionally whether rights are restricted. (e.g. 'All rights reserved', 'Some rights reserved').
element.comment: The copyright symbol and the '(c)' textual representation SHOULD NOT be included in this string. It will be added by software when rendering the notation. Full details about licensing, restrictions, warrantees, etc. goes in the more general 'copyright' element.
element.requirements: Defines the content expected to be rendered in all representations of the artifact.

constraint.human: All FHIR elements must have a @value or children

element.short: When the event definition was approved by publisher
element.definition: The date on which the resource content was approved by the publisher. Approval happens once when the content is officially approved for usage.
element.comment:
The 'date' element may be more recent than the approval date because of minor changes or editorial corrections.

See guidance around (not) making local changes to elements [here](canonicalresource.html#localization).

constraint.human: All FHIR elements must have a @value or children

element.short: When the event definition was last reviewed by the publisher
element.definition: The date on which the resource content was last reviewed. Review happens periodically after approval but does not change the original approval date.
element.comment:
If specified, this date follows the original approval date.

See guidance around (not) making local changes to elements [here](canonicalresource.html#localization).
element.requirements: Gives a sense of how "current" the content is.  Resources that have not been reviewed in a long time may have a risk of being less appropriate/relevant.

constraint.human: All FHIR elements must have a @value or children

element.short: When the event definition is expected to be used
element.definition: The period during which the event definition content was or is planned to be in active use.
element.comment:
The effective period for an event definition  determines when the content is applicable for usage and is independent of publication and review dates. For example, a definition intended to be used for the year 2016 might be published in 2015.

See guidance around (not) making local changes to elements [here](canonicalresource.html#localization).
element.requirements: Allows establishing a transition before a resource comes into effect and also allows for a sunsetting  process when new versions of the event definition are or are expected to be used instead.

For example, it might be a timestamp (e.g. yyyymmdd) if a managed version is not available. There is also no expectation that versions can be placed in a lexicographical sequence. element.comment: Usually an organization but may be an individual. element.requirements: Consumers must be able to determine any legal restrictions on the use of the event definition and/or its content.

Experimental resources might include example instances in implementation guides, instances created solely for testing purposes, etc. If experimental is 'true' for any version of a resource, it should be true for all versions of the resource.  (If experimental changes, then it is being misused or a resource that was never intended for real-world use has unexpectedly changed its purpose.).

resource.name: EvidenceVariable
resource.description: The EvidenceVariable resource describes an element that knowledge (Evidence) is about.
resource.purpose: Need to be able to define and reuse the definition of individual elements of a research question.

element.comment: The EvidenceVariable may be an exposure variable (intervention, condition, or state), a measured variable (outcome or observed parameter), or other variable (such as confounding factor).

element.comment: Asserting this rule set restricts the content to be only understood by a limited set of trading partners. This inherently limits the usefulness of the data in the long term. However, the existing health eco-system is highly fractured, and not yet ready to define, collect, and exchange data in a generally computable sense. Wherever possible, implementers and/or specification writers should avoid using this element. Often, when used, the URL is a reference to an implementation guide that defines these special rules as part of its narrative along with other profiles, value sets, etc.

Not all the content has to be in the base language. The Resource.language should not be assumed to apply to the narrative automatically. If a language is specified, it should it also be specified on the div element in the html (see rules in HTML5 for information about the relationship between xml:lang and the html lang attribute).

element.definition: An absolute URI that is used to identify this evidence variable when it is referenced in a specification, model, design or an instance; also called its canonical identifier. This SHOULD be globally unique and SHOULD be a literal address at which an authoritative instance of this evidence variable is (or will be) published. This URL can be the target of a canonical reference. It SHALL remain the same when the evidence variable is stored on different servers.
element.comment: In some cases, the resource can no longer be found at the stated url, but the url itself cannot change. Implementations can use the meta.source element to indicate where the current master source of the resource can be found.
element.requirements: Allows the evidence variable to be referenced by a single globally unique identifier.

constraint.human: URL should not contain | or # - these characters make processing canonical references problematic

element.short: Additional identifier for the evidence variable
element.definition: A formal identifier that is used to identify this evidence variable when it is represented in other formats, or referenced in a specification, model, design or an instance.
element.requirements: Allows externally provided and/or usable business identifiers to be easily associated with the module.

element.short: Business version of the evidence variable
element.definition: The identifier that is used to identify this version of the evidence variable when it is referenced in a specification, model, design or instance. This is an arbitrary value managed by the evidence variable author and is not expected to be globally unique. For example, it might be a timestamp (e.g. yyyymmdd) if a managed version is not available. There is also no expectation that versions can be placed in a lexicographical sequence.  For more information on versioning knowledge artifacts, refer to the Canonical Resource Management Infrastructure (CRMI) implementation guide artifact versioning discussion (http://hl7.org/fhir/uv/crmi/artifact-lifecycle.html#artifact-versioning).
element.comment: There may be different evidence variable instances that have the same identifier but different versions.  The version can be appended to the url in a reference to allow a reference to a particular business version of the evidence variable with the format [url]|[version]. The version SHOULD NOT contain a '#' - see [Business Version](resource.html#bv-format).

element.definition: Indicates the mechanism used to compare versions to determine which is more current.
element.comment: If set as a string, this is a FHIRPath expression that has two additional context variables passed in - %version1 and %version2 and will return a negative number if version1 is newer, a positive number if version2 is newer, and a 0 if the version ordering can't successfully be determined.

element.definition: A natural language name identifying the evidence variable. This name should be usable as an identifier for the module by machine processing applications such as code generation.
element.comment: The name is not expected to be globally unique. The name should be a simple alphanumeric type name to ensure that it is machine-processing friendly.
element.requirements: Support human navigation and code generation.

element.short: Name for this evidence variable (human friendly)
element.definition: A short, descriptive, user-friendly title for the evidence variable.
element.comment: This name does not need to be machine-processing friendly and may contain punctuation, white-space, etc.

element.short: Title for use in informal contexts
element.definition: The short title provides an alternate title for use in informal descriptive contexts where the full, formal title is not necessary.
element.requirements: Need to be able to reference the content by a short description, but still provide a longer, more formal title for the content.

Allows filtering of artifacts that are appropriate for use versus not. Experimental resources might include example instances in implementation guides, instances created solely for testing purposes, etc. If experimental is 'true' for any version of a resource, it should be true for all versions of the resource.  (If experimental changes, then it is being misused or a resource that was never intended for real-world use has unexpectedly changed its purpose.).

Experimental resources are not expected to be stable and may well have breaking changes without a corresponding change to the 'version' element.

This resource is used to illustrate a specific time-based exchange, not to define in general terms how exchanges can/should occur.

constraint.human: URL should not contain | or # - these characters make processing canonical references problematic

element.short: Additional identifier for the example scenario
element.definition: A formal identifier that is used to identify this example scenario when it is represented in other formats, or referenced in a specification, model, design or an instance.
element.requirements: Allows externally provided and/or usable business identifiers to be easily associated with the module.

element.short: Business version of the example scenario
element.definition: The identifier that is used to identify this version of the example scenario when it is referenced in a specification, model, design or instance. This is an arbitrary value managed by the example scenario author and is not expected to be globally unique. For example, it might be a timestamp (e.g. yyyymmdd) if a managed version is not available. There is also no expectation that versions can be placed in a lexicographical sequence.
element.comment: There may be different example scenario instances that have the same identifier but different versions.  The version can be appended to the url in a reference to allow a reference to a particular business version of the example scenario with the format [url]|[version]. The version SHOULD NOT contain a '#' - see [Business Version](resource.html#bv-format).

element.definition: Indicates the mechanism used to compare versions to determine which is more current.
element.comment: If set as a string, this is a FHIRPath expression that has two additional context variables passed in - %version1 and %version2 and will return a negative number if version1 is newer, a positive number if version2 and a 0 if the version ordering can't be successfully be determined.

element.short: Name for this example scenario (computer friendly)
element.definition: A natural language name identifying the ExampleScenario. This name should be usable as an identifier for the resource by machine processing applications such as code generation.
element.comment: It is not expected that ExampleScenarios will be used to generate code, as they are only examples and not definitional.  However, this element is retained to remain compatible with the canonical resource interface.  Systems are free to omit populating the element.

element.short: Name for this example scenario (human friendly)
element.definition: A short, descriptive, user-friendly title for the ExampleScenario.
element.comment: This name does not need to be machine-processing friendly and may contain punctuation, white-space, etc.

element.definition: The status of this example scenario. Enables tracking the life-cycle of the content.
element.comment:
Allows filtering of example scenarios that are appropriate for use versus not.

See guidance around (not) making local changes to elements [here](canonicalresource.html#localization).
element.isModifierReason: This is labeled as "Is Modifier" because applications should not use a retired ExampleScenario without due consideration

binding.description: The lifecycle status of an artifact.

element.short: For testing only - never for real usage
element.definition: A Boolean value to indicate that this example scenario is authored for testing purposes (or education/evaluation/marketing) and no version of this resource will ever be intended for genuine usage.
element.comment:
Allows filtering of example scenarios that are appropriate for use versus not. Experimental resources might include example instances in implementation guides, instances created solely for testing purposes, etc. If experimental is 'true' for any version of a resource, it should be true for all versions of the resource.  (If experimental changes, then it is being misused or a resource that was never intended for real-world use has unexpectedly changed its purpose.).

Experimental resources are not expected to be stable and may well have breaking changes without a corresponding change to the 'version' element.
element.requirements: Enables experimental content to be developed following the same lifecycle that would be used for a production-level example scenario.
element.meaningWhenMissing: If absent, this resource is treated as though it is not experimental.

element.definition: The date  (and optionally time) when the example scenario was last significantly changed. The date must change when the business version changes and it must change if the status code changes. In addition, it should change when the substantive content of the example scenario changes. (e.g. the 'content logical definition').
element.comment:
The date is often not tracked until the resource is published, but may be present on draft content. Note that this is not the same as the resource last-modified-date, since the resource may be a secondary representation of the example scenario. Additional specific dates may be added as extensions or be found by consulting Provenances associated with past versions of the resource.

See guidance around (not) making local changes to elements [here](canonicalresource.html#localization).

element.short: Name of the publisher/steward (organization or individual)
element.definition: The name of the organization or individual responsible for the release and ongoing maintenance of the example scenario.
element.comment: Usually an organization but may be an individual. The publisher (or steward) of the example scenario is the organization or individual primarily responsible for the maintenance and upkeep of the example scenario. This is not necessarily the same individual or organization that developed and initially authored the content. The publisher is the primary point of contact for questions or issues with the example scenario. This item SHOULD be populated unless the information is available from context.
element.requirements: Helps establish the "authority/credibility" of the example scenario.  May also allow for contact.

element.definition: Contact details to assist a user in finding and communicating with the publisher.
element.comment:
May be a web site, an email address, a telephone number, etc.

See guidance around (not) making local changes to elements [here](canonicalresource.html#localization).

element.short: Natural language description of the ExampleScenario
element.definition: A free text natural language description of the ExampleScenario from a consumer's perspective.
element.comment: This description can be used to capture details such as comments about misuse. It is not a rendering of the ExampleScenario as conveyed in the 'text' field of the resource itself.

element.short: The context that the content is intended to support
element.definition: The content was developed with a focus and intent of supporting the contexts that are listed. These contexts may be general categories (gender, age, ...) or may be references to specific programs (insurance plans, studies, ...) and may be used to assist with indexing and searching for appropriate example scenario instances.
element.comment: When multiple useContexts are specified, there is no expectation that all or any of the contexts apply.
element.requirements: Assist in searching for appropriate content.

element.short: Jurisdiction of the authority that maintains the example scenario (if applicable)
element.definition: A legal or geographic region in which the authority that maintains the resource is operating.  In general, the jurisdiction is also found in the useContext.  The useContext may reference additional jurisdictions because the defining jurisdiction does not necessarily limit the jurisdictions of use.
element.comment: It may be possible for the example scenario to be used in jurisdictions other than those for which it was originally designed or intended.

binding.description: Countries and regions within which this artifact is targeted for use.

element.short: The purpose of the example, e.g. to illustrate a scenario
element.definition: What the example scenario resource is created for. This should not be used to show the business purpose of the scenario itself, but the purpose of documenting a scenario.
element.comment: This element does not describe the usage of the example scenario. Instead, it provides traceability of ''why'' the resource is either needed or ''why'' it is defined as it is.  This may be used to point to source materials or specifications that drove the structure of this example scenario.

element.short: Notice about intellectual property ownership, can include restrictions on use
element.definition: A copyright statement relating to the example scenario and/or its contents. Copyright statements are notices of intellectual property ownership and can include restrictions on the use and publishing of the example scenario.
element.requirements: Consumers must be able to determine any legal restrictions on the use of the example scenario and/or its content.

element.definition: A short string (<50 characters), suitable for inclusion in a page footer that identifies the copyright holder, effective period, and optionally whether rights are restricted. (e.g. 'All rights reserved', 'Some rights reserved').
element.comment: The copyright symbol and the '(c)' textual representation SHOULD NOT be included in this string. It will be added by software when rendering the notation. Full details about licensing, restrictions, warrantees, etc. goes in the more general 'copyright' element.
element.requirements: Defines the content expected to be rendered in all representations of the artifact.

element.definition: A system or person who shares or receives an instance within the scenario.
element.requirements: This is optional to allow for ExampleScenarios that are still draft
element.orderMeaning: The order in which these elements appear is the order in which they are expected to be rendered (in a table, in a diagram, etc.)

constraint.human: actor SHALL have either a type or a definition but not both
actor.key canot be 'OTHER'
Actor should be referenced in at least one operation

element.short: ID or acronym of the actor
element.definition: A unique string within the scenario that is used to reference the actor.
The category of actor - person or system.

binding.description: The type of actor - system or non-system.

element.definition: The human-readable name for the actor used when rendering the scenario.
element.requirements: The title for a particular actor might be more refined/specific than what's found on the definition, if one is provided

element.definition: An explanation of who/what the actor is and its role in the scenario.
element.requirements: The description for a particular actor might be more refined/specific than what's found on the definition, if one is provided

element.definition: The formal definition of the actor in the scenario.
element.comment: The title and description appearing in this resource may differ from that in the formal definition.  The type SHALL be the same.

element.definition: A single data collection that is shared as part of the scenario.

constraint.human: instance.content is only allowed if there are no instance.versions
Instance should be referenced in at least one location
StructureVersion is required if structureType is not FHIR (but may still be present even if FHIR)
Version titles must be unique within an instance
Version keys must be unique within an instance
Instance version should be referenced in at least one operation

element.short: ID or acronym of the instance
element.definition: A unique string within the scenario that is used to reference the instance.
A code indicating the kind of data structure (FHIR resource or some other standard) this is an instance of.
element.comment: This element may be omitted if describing a step that does not involve the sharing of a data structure - e.g. a human action

binding.description: The structure that defines the instance

element.definition: Conveys the version of the data structure instantiated.  I.e. what release of FHIR, X12, OpenEHR, etc. is instance compliant with.
element.meaningWhenMissing: If the structureType is a FHIR resource, then the version is the same FHIR version this ExampleScenario is expressed in.

element.definition: Refers to a profile, template or other ruleset the instance adheres to.
A short descriptive label the instance to be used in tables or diagrams.
An explanation of what the instance contains and what it's for.
Points to an instance (typically an example) that shows the data that would corespond to this instance.
element.comment: If not conveying FHIR data or not using the same version of FHIR as this ExampleScenario instance, the reference must be to a Binary.

element.definition: Represents the instance as it was at a specific time-point.
element.comment: Not used if an instance does not change
element.requirements: Allows representing the 'same' instance as it evolves throughout the scenario.

element.short: ID or acronym of the version
element.definition: A unique string within the instance that is used to reference the version of the instance.
A short descriptive label the version to be used in tables or diagrams.
An explanation of what this specific version of the instance contains and represents.
Points to an instance (typically an example) that shows the data that would flow at this point in the scenario.
element.comment: If not conveying FHIR data or not using the same version of FHIR as this ExampleScenario instance, the reference must be to a Binary.

element.definition: References to other instances that can be found within this instance (e.g. the observations contained in a bundle).
element.requirements: An instance may contain multiple resources - for example, a search response Bundle, a document Bundle, nested contained resources, etc.  In some cases it's useful to be able to talk about these contained instances distinctly, as they may appear in multiple locations in a scenario - sometimes contained, sometimes not.  For example, a scenario may include the creation of an Observation (stand-alone instance) followed by a search that results in a Bundle that contains that same Observation.  The ExampleScenario can highlight the fact that the 'created' instance and 'contained' instance are the same by having the Bundle refer to the same instance id.

constraint.human: versionReference must be specified if the referenced instance defines versions
InstanceReference must be a key of an instance defined in the ExampleScenario
versionReference must be a key of a version within the instance pointed to by instanceReference

element.definition: A reference to the key of an instance found within this one.
A reference to the key of a specific version of an instance in this instance.
element.comment: Required if the referenced instance has versions

element.definition: A group of operations that represents a significant step within a scenario.
element.comment: Some scenarios might describe only one process.
element.orderMeaning: The order in which these elements appear is the order in which they are expected to be rendered (in a table, in a diagram, etc.)

constraint.human: Processes must have steps if ExampleScenario status is active or required

element.definition: A short descriptive label of the process to be used in tables or diagrams.
An explanation of what the process represents and what it does.
Description of the initial state of the actors, environment and data before the process starts.
Description of the final state of the actors, environment and data after the process has been successfully completed.
element.comment: Alternate steps might not result in all post conditions holding

element.definition: A significant action that occurs as part of the process.
element.orderMeaning: The order in which these elements appear is the order in which they are expected to be rendered (in a table, in a diagram, etc.).  It also indicates the order in which the events occur.

constraint.human: Can have a process, a workflow, one or more operations or none of these, but cannot have a combination
constraint.expression: (process.exists() implies workflow.empty() and operation.empty()) and (workflow.exists() implies operation.empty())

constraint.human: Alternative titles must be unique within a step

element.definition: The sequence number of the step, e.g. 1.2.5.
element.comment: If step numbers are simultaneous, they will be the same.  Numbers don't have to be numeric.  E.g. '2c' is a valid step number.  The 'number' should only contain the textual part of the step identifier, not any separating punctuation.  I.e. 'number' should be '2c' not '2c.' or '2c)' or '2c - '.

element.definition: Indicates that the step is a complex sub-process with its own steps.
element.orderMeaning: The order in which these elements appear is the order in which they are expected to be rendered (in a table, in a diagram, etc.)

element.definition: Indicates that the step is defined by a seaparate scenario instance.
The step represents a single operation invoked on receiver by sender.

constraint.human: A definition can only be provided if the type is 'operation'
If specified, initiator must be a key of an actor within the ExampleScenario
If specified, receiver must be a key of an actor within the ExampleScenario

element.definition: The standardized type of action (FHIR or otherwise).
element.comment: This binding is extensible to provide support for non-FHIR interactions as well

element.definition: A short descriptive label the step to be used in tables or diagrams.
If this operation represents the invocation of a FHIR operation, points to the canonical definition of that operation.
The system that invokes the action/transmits the data.
element.comment: This must either be the 'key' of one of the actors defined in this scenario or the special keyword 'OTHER' if the initiator is not one of the actors defined for the scenario.  (Multiple references to 'OTHER' don't necessarily indicate the same actor.)

element.definition: The system on which the action is invoked/receives the data.
element.comment: This must either be the 'key' of one of the actors defined in this scenario or the special keyword 'OTHER' if the receiver is not one of the actors defined for the scenario.  (Multiple references to 'OTHER' don't necessarily indicate the same actor.)  In some cases, receiver could be same as sender if representing a local operation

element.definition: An explanation of what the operation represents and what it does.
element.comment: This should contain information not already present in the process step.  It's more of a description of what the operation in general does - if not already evident from the operation.type

element.definition: If false, the initiator is deactivated right after the operation.
element.comment: De-activation of an actor means they have no further role until such time as they are the recipient of an operation.
element.requirements: The notion of 'activation' in a flow diagram is used to indicate 'who has responsibility/is still doing work'.

element.definition: If false, the receiver is deactivated right after the operation.
element.comment: De-activation of an actor means they have no further role until such time as they are the recipient of an operation.
element.requirements: The notion of 'activation' in a flow diagram is used to indicate 'who has responsibility/is still doing work'.

element.definition: A reference to the instance that is transmitted from requester to receiver as part of the invocation of the operation.
A reference to the instance that is transmitted from receiver to requester as part of the operation's synchronous response (if any).
Indicates an alternative step that can be taken instead of the sub-process, scenario or operation.  E.g. to represent non-happy-path/exceptional/atypical circumstances.
element.orderMeaning: The order in which these elements appear is the order in which they are expected to be rendered (in a table, in a diagram, etc.)

constraint.human: Alternative steps can't have alternatives

element.definition: The label to display for the alternative that gives a sense of the circumstance in which the alternative should be invoked.
A human-readable description of the alternative explaining when the alternative should occur rather than the base step.
Indicates the operation, sub-process or scenario that happens if the alternative option is selected.
element.orderMeaning: The order in which these elements appear is the order in which they are expected to be rendered (in a table, in a diagram, etc.).  It also indicates the order in which the events occur.

element.definition: If true, indicates that, following this step, there is a pause in the flow and the subsequent step will occur at some later time (triggered by some event).

binding.description: Complete, proposed, exploratory, other.

element.short: Relevant time frame for the claim
element.definition: The period for which charges are being submitted.
element.comment: Typically this would be today or in the past for a claim, and today or in the future for preauthorizations and prodeterminations. Typically line item dates of service should fall within the billing period if one is specified.
element.requirements: A number jurisdictions required the submission of the billing period when submitting claims for example for hospital stays or long-term care.

element.definition: The date this resource was created.
element.requirements: Need to record a timestamp for use by both the recipient and the issuer.

element.definition: Individual who created the claim, predetermination or preauthorization.
element.requirements: Some jurisdictions require the contact information for personnel completing claims.
